Lily smiled and hugged Tom. She said, "Thank you, Tom. You are a good friend. I don't need to wear your suit. I just wanted to have fun with you. But I appreciate your offer. You are very generous and nice."

Tom and Lily went back to play. They had a lot of fun and laughed a lot. Tom learned that sharing is caring and that friends are more valuable than things. He still liked his suit, but he liked Lily more. He was happy and grateful.

One day, a little girl came to his shop with her dad. Her dad's car had a big problem and needed Jack's help. The little girl was curious and wanted to see the cars and trucks. The little girl felt sad and hurt. She did not understand why Jack was so mean. She decided to explore the shop by herself. She saw a big truck with a shiny red paint. The little girl was terrified and started to cry. She wanted to get down, but she did not know how. She was stuck on the truck. She wished her dad was there to protect her from Jack.

The little girl smiled and thanked Jack. She forgave him and trusted him. She was happy and eager to learn. She and Jack became friends and had fun together.

The moral of the story is: Don't judge people by their appearance or mood. Be polite and friendly to everyone. You never know who you might meet or what you might learn.

"Uh-oh," they said. "We're sorry, mom!"

"Yuck!" Ben said, dropping the jar. "The worm spit on me!"

Lily laughed. She thought it was funny. She picked up the jar and put it back on the ground.

"Sorry, worm," she said. "We won't bother you anymore."

"Mommy, mommy, open the door!" he shouted. "The worm spit on me!"

Mommy heard him and came to the door. She saw the goo on his hands and the jar on the ground.

"There, that's better," she said. "Next time, be gentle with the worms. They don't like to be shaken."

One day, a chubby cat saw a tap in the garden. He was thirsty, so he walked to the tap and tried to drink some water. But the tap was too high for him, and he could not reach it. He jumped and jumped, but he only hit his head on the tap.

"Ouch!" he said. "This tap is mean. It does not want to give me water."

Then he saw a bird on a branch. The bird was small and thin, and it looked at the cat with pity.

"Hello, cat," the bird said. "Why are you jumping so much?"

"I want to drink water from the tap, but it is too high for me," the cat said.

"Maybe I can help you," the bird said. "If you are nice to me, I can fly to the tap and turn it on for you. Then you can drink water from the ground."

The cat thought for a moment. He was hungry, and he liked to eat birds. But he was also thirsty, and he needed water. He decided to be nice to the bird.

"OK, bird," he said. "You can help me. But you have to promise not to fly away."

"I promise," the bird said. "But you have to promise not to eat me."

"I promise," the cat said.

So the bird flew to the tap and turned it on. Water came out of the tap and fell to the ground. The cat drank some water and felt better. He thanked the bird and kept his promise. He did not eat the bird.

The bird was happy and flew away. He said to the cat, "You are welcome, cat. I hope you learned something today. Sometimes, being nice is better than being mean. And sometimes, you need help from someone who is different from you."

The cat nodded and smiled. He learned something today. He learned to be nice and to ask for help. He also learned that chubby cats and thin birds can be friends. He hoped to see the bird again. He went to sleep under a tree.

"What is that?" Tom asks.

"Can we play with it?" Tom says.

"No, we can't. It is not a toy. It is for real," Lily says.

But Tom does not listen. He runs to the fire truck. He wants to touch it and climb on it. He thinks it is fun.

"Tom, come back! You can't do that!" Lily shouts.

But Tom does not hear her. He is too busy. He opens the door of the fire truck. He sees a lot of buttons and levers. He pushes one of them.

Suddenly, a big spray of water comes out of the hose. It hits Tom and Lily and the other children in the park. They get wet and cold and scared. They cry and scream.

The firemen hear the noise. They run to the fire truck. They see Tom and Lily and the other children. They are angry and worried.

Tom points to Lily. He lies. He says, "She did it. She wanted to play with the fire truck."

Lily is shocked. She says, "No, I didn't. He did it. He ran to the fire truck and pushed the button."

The firemen look at Tom and Lily. They can tell who is telling the truth and who is lying. They scold Tom and make him say sorry. They tell him he was very naughty and dangerous. They tell him he could have hurt someone or caused a fire.

They also tell Lily she was very brave and honest. They thank her for telling the truth. They give her a sticker and a hug.

Mia did not listen. She thought the pole was fun and cool. She chased Tom with the pole. She wanted to make him play with her. She did not care about the germs. She liked the mud and the slime.

"Come on, Tom, don't be a baby!" she urged. She ran faster and faster. She did not see the rock in her way. She tripped and fell. The pole flew out of her hand and landed in the pond. It made a big splash. The ducks flew away. The fish swam away. The water was dirty and disgusting.

Suddenly, she heard her mom calling her name. "Lily, stop!" her mom yelled. Lily turned around and saw her mom waving at her from the other side of the river. Her mom had a big smile on her face and was holding out her arms. Lily knew it was time to go home, so she put down the log and ran towards her mom. They hugged and walked back home together, talking about all the fun things they saw in the forest.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she went outside to play in the snow. She saw some ice on the ground and thought it looked very pretty. 

Suddenly, her friend Tommy came over and asked, "What are you looking at, Lily?" 

"I'm looking at the ice. It's so shiny and cold," Lily replied. 

Tommy was curious and wanted to touch the ice too. He asked, "Can I touch it?" 

Lily thought for a moment and said, "Sure, but be careful. It's slippery." 

Tommy touched the ice and said, "Wow, it's really cold!" 

Lily and Tommy played with the ice for a while longer before going back inside. They both thought it was a fun day playing in the snow. The end.

"I will put my toy here," Fin said to himself. "No one will find it." But Fin didn't know that a thief was watching him. The thief was a sneaky crab named Claw.

The next day, Fin went to the big rock to play with his toy. But his toy was gone! "Oh no," cried Fin. "Where is my toy?" He swam around, looking for it. Then, he saw Claw with his toy.

"Give it back," said Fin. "That's mine!" Claw laughed and ran away. Fin knew he had to be careful to catch the thief. He thought of a plan.

Fin asked his friend, a fast fish named Flash, for help. Together, they swam after Claw. Flash was so fast that Claw couldn't run away. Fin got his toy back, and he learned to be more careful with his things.

Then, Lily noticed something in the bushes. It was the duck! The turkey was so happy to see his friend. They both thanked Lily for her help. The two friends played together again, and Lily went back home, feeling happy that she could help the worried turkey.

Tim agreed. "Yes, Bob. Let's fix it together." They swam to the net and started to fix it. They pulled and pushed the net until it was not enormous anymore.

The other fish in the pond saw what Bob and Tim did. They all cheered and clapped their fins. "Thank you, Bob and Tim!" they said. "You made the pond safe again."

Tim and Jen are twins. They like to play in the park. They have a green ball. They throw the ball to each other and catch it.

One day, a big dog comes to the park. The dog sees the green ball. He runs to the ball and grabs it with his mouth. He runs away with the ball.

Tim and Jen are sad. They want their ball back. They yell at the dog. "Hey, dog! Give us our ball! That is our ball, not yours!"

The dog does not listen. He keeps running with the ball. He goes to the other side of the park. He finds a way out of the park. He goes to the street.

Tim and Jen run after the dog. They are scared. The street is busy. There are many cars and bikes and people. They yell for the dog to stop. But the dog does not stop. He crosses the street.

A nice lady sees the dog and the twins. She stops her car. She gets out of her car. She calls the dog. "Come here, boy! Come here!" She has a treat in her hand.

The dog smells the treat. He drops the ball. He goes to the lady. The lady gives him the treat. She pets him. She sees his collar. She reads his name. "Rex, you are a naughty dog. You should not take things that are not yours."

The lady picks up the ball. She sees Tim and Jen. They are on the sidewalk. They are happy. They see their ball. They thank the lady. "Thank you, lady! Thank you for getting our ball!"

Sara liked to draw. She had many colors and papers. She drew her family, her friends, her toys and her dreams. She was very good at making images with her colors.

One day, she wanted to draw a big image of a castle. She asked her mom for a big paper. Her mom gave her a big paper and said, "Be careful, Sara. This is the last big paper we have. Don't waste it."

Sara said, "OK, mom. I will make a beautiful castle." She started to draw with her colors. She drew a big wall, a big door, a big tower and a big flag. She was very happy with her image.

But then, her little brother Ben came. He saw Sara's image and he liked it. He wanted to draw on it too. He said, "Sara, let me draw. I want to draw a dragon on your castle."

Sara said, "No, Ben. This is my image. You can't draw on it. Go away."

But Ben was very persistent. He did not listen to Sara. He tried to grab her colors. He tried to grab her paper. He said, "Sara, let me draw. I want to draw a dragon on your castle."

Sara was very angry. She said, "No, Ben. This is my image. You can't draw on it. Go away." She pushed him away. She hugged her paper. She cried.

Her mom heard Sara and Ben. She came to see what was wrong. She saw Sara's image and Ben's demand. She said, "Ben, you can't draw on Sara's image. That is not nice. You have to ask her first. And you have to respect her answer. If she says no, you have to accept it."

Ben said, "But mom, I want to draw a dragon on her castle. It will look cool."

Mom said, "I know, Ben. But you can't draw on Sara's image. That is hers. You can draw your own image. Look, I have another paper for you. You can draw a dragon on this paper. And maybe, if you are nice, Sara will let you show her your image."

Ben said, "OK, mom. I will draw my own image. I will draw a dragon on this paper. And I will be nice to Sara."

Mom said, "That's good, Ben. And Sara, I'm sorry that Ben bothered you. Your image is very beautiful. I'm proud of you."

Sara said, "Thank you, mom. I'm sorry that I cried. I worked hard on my image. I don't want Ben to ruin it."

Mom said, "I understand, Sara. You don't have to be sorry. You have the right to protect your image. But you also have to be kind to your brother. He is young and he likes to draw too. Maybe you can share your colors with him. And maybe you can teach him how to draw a castle."

Sara said, "OK, mom. I will share my colors with Ben. And I will teach him how to draw a castle. But he has to promise not to draw on my image."

Mom said, "That's fair, Sara. Ben, do you promise not to draw on Sara's image?"

Ben said, "Yes, mom. I promise not to draw on Sara's image. I will draw on my own paper. And I will learn how to draw a castle from Sara."

Mom said, "That's good, Ben. I'm happy that you and Sara are getting along. Now, let's see your images. I'm sure they are both wonderful."

Lily and Ben were having breakfast with their mom and dad. They liked to eat eggs and toast with jam. Mom cooked the eggs in a pan and put them on plates. She gave one egg to Lily and one to Ben.

"Thank you, Mom," Lily said. She was polite and used her fork and knife to cut her egg. She chewed it slowly and enjoyed the taste.

"Thank you, Mom," Ben said. He was not polite and used his fingers to grab his egg. He chewed it fast and made loud noises. He also dropped some egg on the floor.

"Ben, that's not nice," Mom said. "You should use your fork and knife like Lily. And you should chew quietly and not make a mess."

"But I'm hungry," Ben said. "And I like to chew loud. It's fun."

"No, it's not fun," Dad said. "It's rude and it bothers us. You should be polite and respectful at the table. That's the rule."

Ben pouted and looked at his egg. He saw that Lily had finished hers and was smiling. He felt a little sorry and decided to try to be polite. He picked up his fork and knife and cut his egg. He chewed it quietly and said, "Sorry, Mom and Dad. I'll be polite next time."

Mom and Dad smiled and praised Ben. They were happy that he learned his lesson. They gave him a hug and a kiss and said, "We love you, Ben. And we love you, Lily. You are both good children."

Their mom and dad came and saw Tim and Kim. They were sad and sorry, and they hugged them. They said they were sorry for leaving them alone, and they took them to the doctor. The doctor gave them medicine and bandages, and said they would be okay.

But Tim and Kim learned a lesson. They learned that they should not touch things that are not theirs, and they should not run away from their mom and dad. They learned that being rude can make them hurt and in trouble. They wished they had stayed at home and played with their toys.

One day, she wanted to try something new. She saw a jar of peanut butter on the shelf. She asked her mom if she could have some. Her mom said yes, but be careful. Peanut butter was sticky and thick.

Sara opened the jar and took a spoon. She scooped some peanut butter and put it on a toast. She tried to spread it, but it was hard. It did not glide like butter or jam. It pulled and tore the toast. Sara frowned. She did not like it.

She looked around and saw a cup of milk on the table. She had an idea. She dipped the spoon in the milk and then in the peanut butter. She mixed them together. The peanut butter became smooth and soft. She smiled. She liked it.

She spread the smooth peanut butter on a new toast. She took a bite. It was yummy. She gave some to her mom. Her mom liked it too. They ate the toast and drank the milk. They were happy. Sara learned something new. She liked to try new things.

But then they see a big squirrel. The squirrel is angry. It thinks the acorns are its food. It runs to Anna and Ben and makes a loud noise. It wants the acorns back.

Anna and Ben are scared. They do not want to give the acorns to the squirrel. They think the acorns are their toys. They hold the acorns tight and run away from the squirrel.

The squirrel chases them. It is fast and strong. It jumps on Anna and Ben and tries to take the acorns. Anna and Ben cry and scream. They do not like the squirrel.

They see a bench near the pond. They run to the bench and climb on it. They hope the squirrel will not follow them. They gaze at the pond and see some ducks. The ducks are calm and cool. They swim and quack. They do not care about the acorns.

Anna and Ben wish they were ducks. They think ducks are nice and fun. They throw the acorns into the pond. They do not want the acorns anymore. They want to be friends with the ducks.

The squirrel sees the acorns in the pond. It is sad and angry. It cannot swim and get the acorns. It loses its food. It goes back to the tree and looks for more acorns.

Anna and Ben smile and wave at the ducks. The ducks smile and wave back. They share some bread with the ducks. They are happy. They forget about the squirrel and the acorns. They have new friends.

Lily and Max were twins who liked to look at the stars at night. They had a big book with pictures of stars and planets and moons. Sometimes, their dad would read them stories from the book and teach them new words.

One night, their dad said, "Tonight, we will see something very special in the sky. It is called a comet. A comet is a ball of ice and dust that goes very fast around the sun. Sometimes, it has a long tail of light behind it. Do you want to see it?"

Lily and Max nodded and put on their coats and hats. They followed their dad outside and looked up at the dark sky. They saw many stars twinkling, but they did not see the comet.

"Where is it, dad?" Lily asked.

"It will come soon, Lily. We have to wait a little bit. Comets are not always easy to see. They only come once in a while. We are very lucky to have a chance to see one," their dad said.

They waited and waited. Lily and Max started to feel sleepy. They yawned and rubbed their eyes. They leaned on their dad's shoulders and snuggled close to him.

"Look, there it is!" their dad whispered. He pointed to a bright spot in the sky that moved slowly across the stars. It had a faint tail of light behind it. It was the comet.

Lily and Max opened their eyes wide and gasped. They saw the comet and smiled. It was beautiful and amazing. They learned a new word and a new thing.

"Wow, dad, it is so pretty!" Max said.

"I love it, dad, thank you for showing us!" Lily said.

Their dad hugged them and said, "You're welcome, my sweeties. I'm glad you like it. Now, let's go back inside and get some sleep. You have learned a lot today. Tomorrow, we can look at the book again and learn more about comets and stars."

Lily and Max nodded and followed their dad inside. They were sleepy, but happy. They had seen a comet and learned a new word and a new thing. They dreamed of comets and stars and planets and moons.

Ben and Mia are on a big boat with their mom and dad. They are going to a new place. They are happy to see the water and the fish and the birds. But one day, the sky is dark and the wind is loud. The boat shakes and makes scary noises. Ben and Mia are afraid.

"Mom, dad, what is happening?" Ben asks.

"The boat is in a storm, Ben. It is very strong and dangerous. We have to stay inside and be brave," dad says.

"Will we be okay?" Mia asks.

"We hope so, Mia. We have to pray and trust God. He loves us and he can help us," mom says.

Ben and Mia hug their mom and dad. They close their eyes and pray. They ask God to keep them safe and to stop the storm. They say thank you for their family and their boat.

After a long time, the storm is over. The sky is blue and the sun is bright. The boat is still and quiet. Ben and Mia look out the window and see a big land. It has many houses and trees and people.

"Look, mom, dad, we made it!" Ben says.

"Yes, we did, Ben. That is the port. That is where we will get off the boat and start our new life," dad says.

"Wow, it is so pretty. Can we go and play there?" Mia asks.

"Sure, Mia. But first, we have to say goodbye to the boat and the people who helped us. They are very kind and brave. We are sorry to leave them," mom says.

Ben and Mia nod. They are happy to see the port, but they are also sorry to say goodbye to the boat and the people. They thank God for saving them from the storm and for giving them a new place. They hope to make new friends and have new adventures. They are ready to start their new story.

Tom liked to write. He wrote on paper, on walls, on his toys. He wrote his name, his mom's name, his dog's name. He wrote big and small, fast and slow, neat and messy. He wrote with pens, pencils, crayons, markers. He wrote every day.

One day, Tom found a new thing to write on. It was a tower. A big tower made of blocks. His dad had built it for him. It was brilliant. It had many colors and shapes. It was taller than Tom. It was the best tower ever.

Tom wanted to write on the tower. He thought it would make it more brilliant. He got his favorite marker. It was red. He climbed on a chair. He reached for the top of the tower. He wrote a big T. He smiled.

But then, something bad happened. The tower wobbled. The blocks moved. The tower fell. It made a loud noise. It broke into pieces. Tom fell off the chair. He cried.

His dad heard the noise. He came to see what happened. He saw the broken tower. He saw the red T. He saw Tom on the floor. He was not happy. He was angry. He took the marker from Tom. He said, "No, Tom, no! You don't write on the tower. You write on paper. The tower is not for writing. The tower is for playing. You broke the tower. You made a mess. You are in trouble."

Tom felt sorry. He said, "I'm sorry, dad. I wanted to write on the tower. I thought it would be brilliant. I didn't mean to break it. I love the tower. Can we fix it?"

His dad sighed. He said, "Yes, Tom, we can fix it. But first, you have to clean up the mess. And then, you have to write a sorry note to me. And then, you have to promise to never write on the tower again. Do you understand?"

Tom nodded. He said, "I understand, dad. I will clean up. I will write a sorry note. I will not write on the tower again. I will write on paper. I will be good."

His dad hugged him. He said, "I love you, Tom. But you have to be careful. Writing is good, but not on everything. Some things are not for writing. Some things are for playing. You have to learn the difference."

Tom learned his lesson. He cleaned up the mess. He wrote a sorry note. He did not write on the tower again. He wrote on paper. He played with the tower. He was happy. And his dad was happy too.

Lily was a polite girl who liked to help her mom with the dishes. She always said please and thank you and did not make a mess. One day, it was very cold outside and Lily saw a cat shiver in the snow. She felt sorry for the cat and wanted to help it.

She asked her mom if she could give the cat some milk and a dish to drink from. Her mom said yes and gave her a small dish and a carton of milk. Lily put on her coat and hat and went outside. She found the cat under a tree and called it softly. The cat was scared at first, but then it smelled the milk and came closer.

Lily poured some milk in the dish and put it on the ground. The cat drank the milk and purred. Lily smiled and stroked the cat gently. She said, "You are a nice cat. Do you have a name?" The cat meowed and rubbed its head against her hand. Lily decided to call it Snowy, because it was white like the snow.

She played with Snowy for a while, then she said, "I have to go back inside now. It is too cold for me. But you can stay here and keep the dish. I will come back tomorrow and bring you more milk. Goodbye, Snowy." She gave the cat a hug and ran back to the house.

Her mom was waiting for her and gave her a warm hug too. She said, "You are a kind girl, Lily. You did a good thing for the cat. I am proud of you." Lily felt happy and said, "Thank you, mom. I like to help. And I made a new friend. His name is Snowy. He is a polite cat too. He said thank you with his eyes." Her mom smiled and said, "That is wonderful, Lily. I am sure Snowy is grateful for your friendship. And I am grateful for your help with the dishes. Now let's have some hot chocolate and cookies. You deserve a treat." Lily nodded and said, "Yes, please. That sounds yummy." She and her mom went to the kitchen and enjoyed their snack.

The moral of the story is: Be polite and kind to others, and you will make friends and be happy.

Sam and Mia liked to play with their toy animals. They had a lot of animals, but their favorite was a soft goat. The goat was white and brown and had a bell around its neck. They named him Billy.

One day, Sam and Mia had a fight. They both wanted to play with Billy, but they did not want to share. They pulled and pulled on Billy, trying to take him away from each other. They did not hear the bell jingle or see the goat's eyes look sad.

Suddenly, they heard a rip. They had torn Billy in half. They stopped pulling and looked at what they had done. They felt very bad. They had hurt their friend. They started to cry.

Mom heard them crying and came to see what was wrong. She saw Billy on the floor, torn in two. She felt sorry for Sam and Mia. She hugged them and said, "It's okay. We can fix Billy. But you have to say sorry to each other and to Billy. And you have to learn to share and play nicely."

Sam and Mia said sorry to each other and to Billy. They gave Billy a kiss and handed him to Mom. Mom took Billy to the sewing room and stitched him back together. She made him a new bell and a scarf to cover the tear. She brought him back to Sam and Mia and said, "Here you go. Billy is all better now. He is still your friend. But you have to be gentle and kind to him. He is not a toy. He is a goat."

Sam and Mia thanked Mom and hugged Billy. They felt happy and relieved. They decided to play with Billy together, taking turns and making up stories. Billy felt comfortable and loved. He jingled his bell and smiled.

Anna loved to read books. She read books every day. She read books about animals, and books about stars, and books about magic. She was a gifted reader. She could read big words and long stories.

One day, Anna found a new book in her room. It was a book about trains. Anna liked trains. She opened the book and saw pictures of trains. She saw trains that were fast, and trains that were slow, and trains that were old, and trains that were new. She read the words under the pictures. She learned about the parts of the trains, and the places they went, and the people who rode them.

Anna turned the page and saw a picture of a very special train. It was a train that had steam. The steam came out of a big pipe on the top of the train. The steam made the train move. The train was called a steam engine. Anna read the words under the picture. She learned that the steam engine was very old, and very rare, and very beautiful. She learned that the steam engine was in a museum, and that only a few people could see it.

Anna wished she could see the steam engine. She wished she could touch it, and hear it, and smell it. She wished she could ride it. She closed the book and put it on her bed. She went to sleep and dreamed of the steam engine.

The next day, Anna woke up and saw her mom smiling at her. She said, "Anna, I have a surprise for you. We are going to the museum today. And guess what? They have a steam engine there. And guess what else? You can ride it. It is a special day for gifted readers like you. You can read the book on the way there. Are you ready?"

Anna was so happy. She hugged her mom and said, "Yes, yes, yes! Thank you, thank you, thank you!" She grabbed the book and ran to the car. She could not wait to see the steam engine. She knew it would be the best day ever.

One day, a little boy named Tom was playing with his toy cars in his room. He liked to make loud noises and pretend they were racing and crashing. He did not hear his mom call him for dinner. He was too busy having fun.

His mom called him again and again, but he did not listen. He thought he could play for a little longer. He did not know that his mom had cooked his favorite food: chicken and rice. He did not know that his mom was getting angry and sad.

Soon, his mom came to his room and saw him still playing. She was very fierce. She took away his toy cars and said, "Tom, you are a bad boy. You did not come when I called you. You did not respect me. You did not care about the food I made for you. Now you have no toy cars and no dinner. Go to bed without any story."

Tom felt very sorry. He realized he had made a big mistake. He had hurt his mom's feelings and missed his favorite food. He wished he had listened to her call. He cried and said, "Mom, I am sorry. I love you. Please forgive me. Please give me back my toy cars and my dinner. Please read me a story."

His mom saw that he was sincere. She felt sorry for him too. She hugged him and said, "Tom, I forgive you. But you have to learn to obey me when I call you. It is for your own good. I love you too. You can have your toy cars and your dinner. But you have to eat fast and brush your teeth. Then I will read you a story."

Tom was very happy. He thanked his mom and did what she said. He enjoyed his dinner and his story. He learned his lesson. He decided to always listen to his mom's call. He knew she wanted the best for him. He knew she was not fierce, but kind.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to splash in the water fountain and make funny noises. They saw a big box near the fountain. It had a picture of a puzzle on it.

"Look, a puzzle!" Lily said. "Let's open it and see what it is."

They opened the box and found many pieces of different colors and shapes. They tried to put them together, but it was hard. They did not know what the puzzle was.

"Maybe it is a flower, or a car, or a dinosaur," Ben guessed.

"Or maybe it is something unknown, something we never saw before," Lily said.

They worked on the puzzle for a long time, but they could not finish it. They got tired and hungry. They decided to leave the puzzle and go home.

"Maybe we can come back tomorrow and try again," Lily said.

"Or maybe someone else will find it and solve it," Ben said.

They put the pieces back in the box and left it near the fountain. They waved goodbye to the water and the puzzle and went home with their mom. They wondered what the unknown puzzle was.

Lily and Max love to play with their puppy, Spot. Spot is a black and white dog who likes to run and jump and lick their faces. One day, Lily and Max decide to race with Spot in the park. They each hold a stick and call Spot to follow them.

Lily runs fast, but Max runs faster. He is almost at the finish line when he sees Spot behind him. Spot is panting and wagging his tail, but he cannot catch up. Max feels sorry for Spot. He stops and waits for him. He gives him the stick and says, "Good boy, Spot. You are a great racer."

Lily catches up with them and smiles. She is proud of her brother. She says, "You are very generous, Max. You let Spot win the race. You are a good friend to him." She hugs Max and Spot and gives them each a kiss.

Tom and Sue are playing with their toys in the living room. They have a lot of fun with their cars, dolls, blocks and books. But they also like to see what Mom and Dad have in their room. Sometimes they find shiny things, soft things, or funny things that they want to play with.

One day, when Mom and Dad are out, they sneak into their room and look around. They see a big box on the bed. It has a bow and a tag that says "Do not open until Christmas". Tom and Sue are very curious and nosy. They want to know what is inside the box.

"Let's open it and see," Tom says. "Maybe it is a toy for us."

"No, we can't," Sue says. "Mom and Dad will be mad. They said we have to wait."

"But they won't know," Tom says. "We can open it and then put it back. Just for a minute."

Sue thinks for a moment. She also wants to see what is in the box. She nods and says, "Okay, but we have to be quick and careful."

They climb on the bed and pull the bow. They lift the lid and peek inside. They see a big, fluffy, white teddy bear. It has a red nose and a green scarf. It looks very cute and cozy.

"Wow, look at that!" Tom says. "It is so nice. Can I hold it?"

"Me too, me too," Sue says. "Let me touch it."

They take the teddy bear out of the box and hug it. They feel its soft fur and squeeze its nose. They laugh and smile. They forget about the time and the box.

But then they hear a sound. It is the door. Mom and Dad are back. They hear their footsteps and their voices.

"Oh no, we have to put it back!" Sue says. "Hurry, hurry!"

They try to put the teddy bear back in the box. But it is too big and too fluffy. It does not fit. They push and pull, but it is no use. The box is too small and the lid is too tight.

They hear Mom and Dad coming closer. They panic and hide under the bed. They hope Mom and Dad will not see the box.

But Mom and Dad do see the box. They see the bow is gone and the lid is open. They see the teddy bear sticking out. They know what Tom and Sue have done.

They look at each other and smile. They have a plan. They pretend to be angry and surprised.

"Who opened this box?" Mom says. "Who was so nosy and naughty?"

"It was not us," Dad says. "It must have been someone else."

They look under the bed and see Tom and Sue. They are scared and sorry. They know they have been caught.

"Tom, Sue, come out here," Dad says. "We have to talk to you."

Tom and Sue come out from under the bed. They hang their heads and say, "We are sorry, Mom and Dad. We were just curious. We wanted to see what was in the box."

Mom and Dad hug them and say, "We know, we know. We were also curious when we were little. But you have to learn to be patient and respectful. The box was a surprise for you. It was a gift from Grandma and Grandpa. They wanted you to have this teddy bear for Christmas. They made it with love and care. They wanted you to be happy and warm."

Tom and Sue feel bad and ashamed. They say, "We are sorry, Grandma and Grandpa. We did not mean to ruin your surprise. We love you and your teddy bear."

Mom and Dad smile and say, "It's okay, Tom and Sue. We forgive you. And we are sure Grandma and Grandpa will forgive you too. They love you very much. But you have to promise us something. You have to promise to wait until Christmas to open your other gifts. Can you do that?"

Tom and Sue nod and say, "Yes, Mom and Dad. We promise. We will wait until Christmas. We will not be nosy and naughty again."

Mom and Dad say, "Good. We are proud of you. Now, why don't you take your teddy bear and play with it in the living room? You can name it and dress it and make it your friend. It is yours to keep and enjoy."

Tom and Sue say, "Thank you, Mom and Dad. Thank you, Grandma and Grandpa. We love you and your teddy bear."

They take their teddy bear and run to the living room. They are happy and grateful. They have learned a lesson. They have also gained a new friend. They name it Snow

One day, Jill wanted to wash Rose's hair. She thought it was dirty and needed water. She took Rose to the sink in the kitchen. She turned on the tap and put Rose under the water. She rubbed her hair with soap and rinsed it.

But something went wrong. The water was too hot and too strong. It burned Rose's hair and face. It made her dress wet and torn. It broke her delicate face. Rose was ruined.

Jill screamed and cried. She dropped Rose in the sink and ran to her mom. She told her what happened. Her mom was angry and sad. She said Jill was naughty and careless. She said she could not fix Rose. She said Jill had to throw her away.

Jill felt very sorry and very sad. She lost her favorite doll. She wished she had not washed her hair. She wished she had been more gentle and careful. She learned a hard lesson. She never played with the sink again.

Lily and Ben were best friends. They liked to play together in the street. They had a big box of toys and they shared them nicely.

One day, they found a new toy in the box. It was a big bowl and a spoon. Lily and Ben wanted to play with it. They decided to make a cake.

They went to the kitchen and asked Mom for some flour, sugar, eggs and milk. Mom gave them the ingredients and told them to be careful and not make a mess.

Lily and Ben took the bowl and the spoon to the street. They poured the flour, the sugar, the eggs and the milk into the bowl. They started to mix them with the spoon.

"Mix, mix, mix!" they said. "We are making a cake!"

But the cake did not look good. It was runny and sticky and lumpy. It spilled over the bowl and onto the street.

"Uh-oh," said Lily. "This is not a good cake. Maybe we need something else."

She looked around and saw some dirt, some grass, some flowers and some rocks. She thought they would make the cake better. She picked them up and put them in the bowl.

"Mix, mix, mix!" she said. "Now the cake is better!"

But Ben did not like Lily's idea. He thought the cake was worse. He did not want dirt, grass, flowers and rocks in his cake. He wanted a yummy cake.

"No, no, no!" he said. "This is a bad cake. Take them out!"

He tried to take out the dirt, the grass, the flowers and the rocks from the bowl. But Lily did not let him. She was stubborn. She wanted her cake.

"Stop, stop, stop!" she said. "This is my cake. Leave it alone!"

They started to fight over the bowl and the spoon. They pulled and pushed and shouted. They made a bigger mess.

Mom heard the noise and came to the street. She saw Lily and Ben and the bowl and the spoon and the cake. She was not happy.

"What are you doing?" she asked. "This is not a cake. This is a disaster. You have to clean up this mess right now!"

Lily and Ben stopped fighting. They looked at Mom and then at the cake. They felt sorry. They knew they had been naughty.

"Sorry, Mom," they said. "We wanted to make a cake, but we did not know how."

Mom sighed. She took the bowl and the spoon and the cake. She threw them in the trash. She gave Lily and Ben a cloth and a bucket of water. She told them to wash the street.

Lily and Ben did as Mom said. They washed the street. They said sorry to each other. They hugged and made up.

They learned their lesson. They decided to never mix dirt, grass, flowers and rocks with flour, sugar, eggs and milk again. They decided to ask Mom to teach them how to make a real cake next time.

One day, Lily went to school. She was happy to see her teacher and her friends. Her teacher said they would do math today. Lily smiled. She took out her math book and opened it.

She whispered to her friend, Ben. "Ben, I don't like the new math problems. They are scary. Can we do the old math problems instead?"

Ben looked at Lily. He saw that she was scared. He felt sorry for her. He said, "Lily, I know you like the old math problems. But the new math problems are not scary. They are just different. They are fun and easy, too. You can do them. I will help you. Just follow me."

She was surprised. The new math problems were not scary. They were fun and easy. She liked them. She smiled. She thanked Ben. She thanked her teacher. She was proud of herself. She liked math.

Sara and Ben ran away from the table and the bees. They ran to their mom who was sitting on a bench. She saw their faces covered with sugar and their eyes full of tears. She hugged them and asked them what happened.

They told her the truth and said they were sorry. She was not happy but she was glad they were safe. She told them they should never take things that are not theirs and they should read signs before they touch anything. She said the sugar was for the bees who needed it to make honey. She said the bees were angry because they thought Sara and Ben wanted to steal their food.

Sara and Ben learned their lesson. They said they would never take sugar or anything else from the park again. They said they would be kind to the bees and other animals. They said they would listen to their mom and read signs. They wiped their faces and drank some clear water. They felt better and went back to play in the park.

"Look, Lily, I found a mitten!" Ben said. He picked up a red mitten from the ground. It was very soft and warm. He tried to put it on his hand, but it was too small. It was very tight.

"Surprise!" The snowman said. He lifted his arm and showed Lily her other mitten. He had hidden it behind his back. He winked at her.

"Wow, snowman. You are amazing. Thank you for my mitten. Do you want to play with us?" Lily asked. She was very excited.

"Yes, please. I would love to play with you. You are very nice. You made me happy." The snowman said. He gave Lily her mitten and hugged her.

Tom and Sam were friends. They liked to play with toys and run in the park. One day, they saw a monkey at the zoo. The monkey was funny and smart. He made faces and jumped on the trees.

Tom and Sam wanted to play with the monkey. They asked their mom and dad, "Please, can we play with the monkey?" But their mom and dad said, "No, the monkey is not a toy. He is a wild animal. He can bite and scratch. You have to stay away from him."

Tom and Sam were sad. They did not listen to their mom and dad. They waited until they were not looking. Then they ran to the monkey cage. They opened the door and went inside. They tried to hug and pet the monkey.

But the monkey did not like that. He was scared and angry. He bit Tom on the hand and scratched Sam on the face. Tom and Sam cried out loud. They ran out of the cage. Their mom and dad heard them and came to help. They saw the blood and the tears. They were very mad and worried.

The wolf felt the fire and screamed. He jumped out of the chimney and ran away. He never came back. The three pigs were safe and happy. They lived in the brick house together. The end."

Ben felt sorry. He saw that he hurt Lily's feelings. He did not mean to do that. He wanted to make her happy again.

"I'm sorry, Lily," he said. "I was jealous of your tower. It was very pretty. I wanted to have red blocks too. Can we share the blocks and build a new tower together?"

Lily stopped crying. She looked at Ben. She saw that he was sorry. She decided to forgive him.

Ben nodded. He put the spike away. He hugged Lily and said, "Thank you, Lily. You are a good friend. Let's make the best tower ever."

He smiled and asked the frog "What are you doing here?", but the frog said nothing. Jimmy thought the frog was lonely, so he asked "Do you want to come with me?"

The frog hopped up and down, as if he was saying yes. Jimmy laughed and picked the frog up carefully.

Suddenly, he heard a voice. "You can't take the frog!"

Jimmy looked around and saw an old man with a big beard. 

The man said "That's my pet, you need to give him back!"

Jimmy thought for a moment and then put the frog back down. The frog hopped away happily. Jimmy smiled and said goodbye to the old man.

Lily played with the monkey all day. She made it clap its hands and dance to the music. The other toys watched and enjoyed the show. At the end of the day, Lily put the monkey back in its organized spot. She gave it a hug and said goodnight. The monkey was very happy to have a friend like Lily.

The boot baked the cake in the oven. But, the boot did not know how long to bake the cake. The cake burned and the house filled with smoke. The boot was sad. It could not share the cake with the town. The town was sad too. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to sing and dance all day long. One day, her mother took her to a lecture about animals. The lady who gave the lecture was very bossy and Lily didn't like her at all. 

During the lecture, Lily got bored and started to clap her hands loudly. The lady got angry and told her to stop. Lily didn't listen and kept clapping.

When they reached the top of the mountain, the villagers were startled to find a dragon sleeping peacefully. They knew that the dragon was the source of the rumour.

The villagers were so relieved to see that the dragon meant them no harm. They thanked their luck that the threat was only a peaceful dragon. Ever since, the villagers have believed that there is nothing to worry about on the mountain.

A delicious flame colored fruit was hanging from a cactus! He had never seen anything so bright and yummy in all his life. He quickly reached out to eat the fruit, but it disappeared!

He asked the cactus where the fruit had gone and the cactus said, "I ate it. You see, I'm really hungry too. I'm sorry you didn't get to eat it". 

The cactus and the hungry cactus became friends after that. They would chat and share stories about their journeys as the days went by. From that day on, the hungry cactus was never hungry again!

Mom smiled and kissed her. She said, "I love you too, Sara. I am glad you are safe. I hope you learned your lesson. Now, let's go to bed. Tomorrow, we can draw together. We can use crayons. They are better than pencils. They do not break or freeze."

They packed their equipment in their backpacks and said goodbye to the park. They walked with their mom and dad to the car. On the way, they saw a man who was bald. He had no hair on his head. He smiled at them and said hello.

Lily and Max were curious. They asked their mom and dad why the man was bald. Their mom and dad explained that some people have hair and some people don't. They said that hair is not important, and that what matters is how kind and friendly people are.

Lily and Max nodded and agreed. They said that the bald man was very nice. They waved at him and he waved back. Then they got in the car and drove home. They were happy and sleepy. They yawned again and fell asleep. They dreamed of the park and the bald man.

Lily was a big girl now. She could wear pants like her brother Tom. She liked her new pants. They were blue and soft and had pockets. She put her toy car in one pocket and her candy in another.

She wanted to show her pants to her friend Anna. She ran to Anna's house and knocked on the door. Anna's mom opened the door and smiled. "Hello, Lily. Welcome to our house. Do you want to play with Anna?"

Lily nodded and said, "Yes, please. Look at my pants. They are new and nice. Do you like them?"

Anna's mom said, "They are very nice, Lily. I like them a lot. Come in, Anna is in her room."

Lily followed Anna's mom to Anna's room. She saw Anna sitting on the floor with her dolls. She said, "Hi, Anna. Look at my pants. They are new and nice. Do you like them?"

Anna looked at Lily's pants and frowned. She said, "No, I don't like them. They are blue and boring. I like pink and sparkly. Your pants are ugly."

Lily felt sad and angry. She said, "No, they are not ugly. They are nice and soft and have pockets. You are mean and rude. I don't want to play with you."

She took out her candy from her pocket and put it in her mouth. She hoped it would make her feel better. But the candy was bitter and sour. It made her face twist and her tongue hurt. She spit it out and said, "Yuck! This candy is bad. It tastes like dirt."

Anna laughed and said, "That's what you get for wearing ugly pants. You have bad candy. My candy is sweet and yummy. Do you want some?"

Lily shook her head and said, "No, thank you. I don't want your candy. I don't want anything from you. You are not my friend. You are mean and bitter. I'm going home."

She grabbed her toy car from her other pocket and ran out of Anna's room. She said goodbye to Anna's mom and left the house. She ran back to her own house and hugged her mom. She told her what happened and cried. Her mom said, "I'm sorry, Lily. Anna was not nice to you. She should have been kind and polite. You don't need friends like that. You have other friends who like you and your pants. Your pants are lovely and so are you. I love you, Lily."

Lily smiled and said, "I love you too, mom. Thank you for my pants. They are my favorite." She wiped her tears and felt better. She decided to call her other friend Ben and ask him to play. She hoped he would like her pants and her candy. She hoped he would be nice and sweet. She hoped he would welcome her.

Sara liked to read books. She had many books with pictures and words. She read them every day. She read them to her toys and her cat. She read them to her mom and dad. She read them to herself.

One day, Sara went to the farm with her class. She saw many animals. She saw cows and pigs and chickens. She saw horses and sheep and ducks. And she saw a goat. The goat was white and brown. He had horns and a beard. He looked charming.

Sara wanted to read to the goat. She took her book from her backpack. She walked to the goat. She said, "Hello, goat. Do you want to hear a story?" The goat said, "Baa." Sara thought that meant yes. She opened her book and started to read.

But the goat was not interested in the story. He was interested in the book. He sniffed the book. He licked the book. He bit the book. He tore the book. Sara was shocked. She said, "No, goat! Stop! That is my book! You are ruining it!" The goat said, "Baa." He did not stop.

Sara cried. She ran to her teacher. She said, "Teacher, teacher, the goat ate my book! He was very bad!" The teacher said, "Oh, Sara, I'm sorry. The goat did not know. He thought it was food. He likes to eat paper. Come, I have another book for you. It is the same as yours. You can read it to me." Sara said, "Thank you, teacher. You are very kind. But I don't want to read to the goat anymore. He is not charming. He is naughty." The teacher said, "I understand. Maybe next time you can read to another animal. How about the duck? He is very charming." Sara said, "Maybe. But I think I like the cat better. He is very charming. And he does not eat books." The teacher said, "That is true. The cat is very charming. And he likes to listen to stories. Let's go and find him." Sara said, "Yes, let's go." And they went.

Lily was curious. She wanted to learn new things and hear stories and jokes. She decided to try to play with the old pig. She walked slowly to the corner and said, "Hello, pig. My name is Lily. Do you want to be my friend?"

The old pig opened one eye and looked at Lily. He saw her bright smile and her big eyes. He felt a warm feeling in his heart. He said, "Hello, Lily. My name is Oink. Of course I want to be your friend. Come closer and sit with me. I have many things to tell you."

Lily and Oink became friends. They talked and laughed and snorted and oinked. They shared stories and jokes and secrets. They had fun and learned from each other. Lily was happy. Grandma hugged Lily and Oink and said, "You are very welcome, my dear. I am happy to see you happy. You are both very good pigs."

Jane's mom heard her cries and came to her rescue. She said, "Jane, why are you so frightened?" Jane said, "I heard a loud roar from the forest and it scared me". 

Her mom assured her that everything was alright and said, "It was just a foolish owl hooting its call". Jane felt better and hugged her mom. She realized that it was foolish of her to be scared of the owl. 

With courage, Jane decided to explore the forest with her mom. She learnt that sometimes being brave was worth the adventure!

She calls her mom. She says, "Mom, can we go to Tom's home? He is in the flood. He is sad."

Her mom says, "Yes, we can go. But we have to be careful. The water is dangerous. We have to take the car."

They get in the car. They drive to Tom's home. They see Tom and his mom outside. They are wet and cold.

Sue runs to Tom. She hugs him. She says, "Tom, I am here. I am your friend. I will comfort you."

Tom stops crying. He smiles. He says, "Thank you, Sue. You are a good friend. You make me happy."

Sue's mom gives Tom and his mom some blankets and some food. She says, "You can come to our home. You can stay with us until the water goes away."

Tom and his mom say, "Thank you, Sue's mom. You are very kind. You help us a lot."

They all go to Sue's home. They are warm and dry. They are happy. They are friends.

The moral of the story is: Friends comfort each other in times of trouble. Friends share what they have. Friends are better than regular things.

Jill and Tom were twins who liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a shiny copper coin on the ground. They both wanted it, so they ran to pick it up. But they got there at the same time, and each grabbed one side of the coin.

"Mine!" Jill said.

"No, mine!" Tom said.

They pulled and tugged, but the coin did not move. They stared at each other, angry and stubborn. They did not notice the big dog that was watching them from behind a tree. The dog liked shiny things, and he wanted the coin too. He was persistent, and he waited for his chance.

Suddenly, the dog barked and jumped out of the tree. He ran towards Jill and Tom, who were still holding the coin. They were scared and let go of the coin. The dog snatched it in his mouth and ran away.

"Hey, come back!" Jill and Tom shouted. They chased the dog, but he was too fast. They lost sight of him and the coin.

They stopped and looked at each other. They felt silly and sorry. They hugged and said, "I'm sorry. Let's share next time."

They walked back to the park, holding hands. They learned a lesson that day: it is better to share than to fight. And to watch out for dogs that like shiny things.

"Let's whisper, so Mom won't hear us," Lily said. She climbed on a chair and reached for the jar.

"Be careful, Lily," Max said. He stood on his toes and watched her.

Lily opened the jar and smelled the pepper. It made her sneeze. "Achoo!"

Max giggled. He wanted to smell it too. He took the jar from Lily and put it near his nose. He sneezed too. "Achoo!"

The pepper flew out of the jar and covered their faces and clothes. They looked like snowmen.

Mom heard the noise and came to the kitchen. She saw Lily and Max and the pepper everywhere. She was not happy.

"What are you doing, you silly kids?" she asked. "Pepper is not for playing. It is for cooking. It is tough and spicy. It can hurt your eyes and nose."

Lily and Max felt sorry. They said sorry to Mom. They helped her clean the kitchen. They learned their lesson. They never played with pepper again.

One day, her brother Tom found her diary. He was bored and curious. He took the key and opened the diary. He read some of the pages and laughed. He saw that Sara wrote that she liked Ben, a boy in her class. He also saw that Sara wrote that she was frustrated with Tom for breaking her doll.

Tom decided to play a prank on Sara. He wrote in her diary with a big marker. He wrote "Sara loves Ben" and "Tom is the best" and "Sara is a baby". He also drew some silly pictures. He closed the diary and put it back under the pillow.

When Sara came back from school, she wanted to write in her diary. She took it out and saw the marker. She opened it and saw what Tom wrote. She was very angry and sad. She ran to Tom and shouted.

"Tom, you are mean! You ruined my diary! How could you do this?"

Tom smirked and said, "I was just having fun. Don't be so mad. It's just a diary. You should thank me for making it more interesting."

Sara felt like crying. She threw the diary at Tom and ran to her room. She slammed the door and sobbed. She wished she had a nicer brother. She wished she had a new diary. She wished Tom would say sorry. But he didn't. He just laughed and played with his toys. Sara felt very lonely and hurt. She didn't want to talk to Tom ever again.

Lily and Ben were twins. They liked to play with their toys and books. One day, they saw a big box in the hall. It had a sticker that said "Happy Birthday, Mom". They wondered what was inside.

They opened the box and found a lot of things. There were clothes, shoes, a bag, and a book. But there was also something weird. It was a candle, but it was not like any candle they had seen before. It was long and thin and had many colors. It also had a button on the side.

Lily and Ben were curious. They took the candle and went to their room. They put it on the table and pressed the button. Suddenly, the candle started to sing and dance. It sang a funny song about ordering pizza and cake. It also moved its arms and legs and spun around.

Lily and Ben laughed and clapped. They thought the candle was very fun and cool. They joined the song and danced with the candle. They did not hear Mom coming up the stairs.

Mom opened the door and saw the mess. She saw the box, the clothes, the shoes, the bag, and the book. She also saw the candle, the twins, and the song. She was very surprised and angry.

"What are you doing?" she asked. "This is my birthday present. You should not open it. And what is that candle? It is very weird."

Lily and Ben stopped and looked at Mom. They felt sorry and scared. They did not know the candle was for Mom. They did not know it was weird.

"We are sorry, Mom," they said. "We just wanted to see what was inside. We did not mean to make a mess. We like the candle. It is very fun and cool. It sings and dances. Do you want to order pizza and cake?"

Mom sighed and smiled. She was not angry anymore. She hugged the twins and kissed them. She said, "It is okay. I forgive you. You are very sweet and cute. I like the candle too. It is very fun and cool. But it is also a special candle. It is a magic candle. It can make wishes come true. Do you want to make a wish?"

Lily and Ben nodded and smiled. They said, "Yes, we do. We wish for pizza and cake. And we wish for a happy birthday for you, Mom."

Mom said, "That is a very nice wish. Thank you, my loves. Let's blow the candle together and see what happens."

They blew the candle and waited. Then they heard a knock on the door. It was the pizza man. He had a big box of pizza and a cake. He said, "Someone ordered pizza and cake for a birthday. Is this the right address?"

Mom, Lily, and Ben looked at each other and laughed. They said, "Yes, it is. Thank you, magic candle. Thank you, pizza man. Come in and join us. We have a party to celebrate."

"Wow, look at all the white!" Lily said, as she ran to touch the snow. "It's so cold and soft!"

"Vroom, vroom, I want to slide on the snow!" Ben said, as he grabbed a sled. "It's so fast and fun!"

Lily and Ben had a great time at the snow park. They made snowmen, snow angels, and snowballs. They also went on a journey on a train that went around the park. They saw penguins, polar bears, and snowflakes.

But soon, the sun came out and the snow started to melt. Lily and Ben noticed that their snowmen were getting smaller and smaller.

"Mom, what's happening to our snowmen?" Lily asked, with a sad voice.

"They're melting, honey. That's what happens when snow gets warm. It turns into water," Mom explained.

"But I don't want them to melt! I want them to stay with us!" Ben cried, as he hugged his snowman.

"I know, sweetie. But we can't keep them. They belong to the snow park. We have to say goodbye to them and go home," Mom said, as she hugged Ben and Lily.

Lily and Ben looked at their snowmen and said goodbye. They thanked them for being their friends and making them happy. They also took a picture of them, so they could remember them.

As they walked to the car, Lily and Ben realized that they had something in common. They both loved the snow and the snowmen. They smiled at each other and held hands.

"Ben, I'm sorry I said you were different. You're my brother and I love you," Lily said.

"Lily, I'm sorry I said you were different. You're my sister and I love you," Ben said.

Mom smiled and said, "You see, kids, you can be different and still love each other. That's what makes you special. And you know what? The snowmen may have melted, but they're still with us. They're in our hearts and in our memories."

Mia took Bobo and made him dance. Ben took Bobo and made him sing. They had fun with Bobo. But they did not give him back to Lila. They kept passing him to each other. Lila felt sad. She wanted to play with Bobo too. She said, "Friends, can I have Bobo back? He is tired. He needs a rest."

Mia and Ben did not listen. They said, "No, we want to play with Bobo more. He is so cool. He can do anything."

Bobo heard Lila. He felt sorry for her. He wanted to go back to her. He was her robot. He said, "Friends, please give me back to Lila. She is my owner. She is nice to me. She carries me in her backpack. She takes care of me."

Mia and Ben were surprised. They did not know Bobo could talk like that. They realized they were being rude. They said, "Sorry, Lila. Sorry, Bobo. We did not mean to hurt you. You are right. Bobo is your robot. You are his owner. You are nice to him. You carry him in your backpack. You take care of him."

They gave Bobo back to Lila. Lila hugged Bobo. She said, "Thank you, Bobo. You are a good robot. You are my friend. I love you."

Bobo said, "I love you too, Lila. You are a good owner. You are my friend. I am happy with you."

Lila, Mia and Ben smiled. They learned to share and respect each other's toys. They played together with Bobo and the ball. They had fun.

The end.

After a while, Lily's mom said, "It's time to move on, sweetie. We have to get back home." Lily was sad to leave the oasis, but she knew they had to go. "Goodbye, oasis," she said. "I'll come back to see you again one day."

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Spot. Spot loved to run and play, but he had a problem. His heel hurt and he couldn't run as fast as he wanted to. One day, Spot met a friendly cat who told him a joke. Spot laughed so hard that he forgot about his sore heel.

"Tom, that is not snow. That is salt. Salt is not good to play with. Salt can hurt your mouth and make you thirsty. You should put the salt back in the jar," she said, being honest.

"No, Lily, you are wrong. Salt is snow. Salt is fun to play with. You are just jealous of my snow. Go away and leave me alone," he said, being rude.

"Lily, you are right. Salt is not snow. Salt is salt. I was wrong. I was rude. I am sorry. Can we still be friends?" he said, being sorry.

Lily smiled. She forgave Tom. She was happy.

"Wow, that's cool!" Anna said. "Can I try it?"

"Sure, here you go." Ben handed her the flashlight. Anna turned it on and off, making funny shadows on the tent wall.

Suddenly, they heard a loud roar outside. They felt the ground shake and the tent flap. They were scared.

"What is that?" Anna whispered.

"I don't know," Ben whispered back. "Maybe it's a bear or a lion or a dinosaur."

They peeked out of the tent and saw a big truck parked next to the tree. It had a powerful engine and a loud horn. It was not a bear or a lion or a dinosaur. It was a garbage truck.

The garbage truck driver saw them and smiled. He waved at them and said, "Hi, kids! Don't be afraid. I'm just here to collect the trash. Do you like my truck?"

Anna and Ben recognized the driver. He was Mr. Lee, their neighbor. They felt relieved and happy. They waved back and said, "Hi, Mr. Lee! We like your truck. It's very powerful."

Mr. Lee laughed and said, "Thank you. It's a good truck. It helps me keep the park clean. Do you like your tent?"

Anna and Ben nodded and said, "Yes, we love our tent. It's very fun."

Anna and Ben said, "OK, Mr. Lee. Thank you. Bye!"

Mr. Lee said, "Bye, kids. See you later." He got back in his truck and drove away.

Anna and Ben went back to their tent. They decided to play some more. They turned on the flashlight and pretended they were exploring a cave. They had a lot of fun. They liked their tent. And they liked Mr. Lee. He was a nice man. And he had a powerful truck.

One day, Lila saw a firework in the garage. It was shiny and colorful and had a long string. She wanted to play with it and see what it could do. She did not ask her mom and dad, because she thought she knew everything. She took the firework and ran to the backyard.

She found a stick and tied the string to it. She lit the string with a match and threw the stick in the air. She wanted to see the firework send sparks and make a loud noise. She thought it would be fun and pretty.

But the firework did not do what she expected. It flew back to the ground and landed near a pile of leaves. The leaves caught fire and started to burn. Lila was scared and did not know what to do. She ran to the house and called for her mom and dad.

Her mom and dad came out and saw the fire. They quickly got a hose and put out the fire. They were angry and worried. They asked Lila what she had done and why she did not ask them first. Lila felt sorry and ashamed. She told them the truth and said she was sorry.

Her mom and dad hugged her and said they were glad she was safe. They said firework was not a toy and could be very dangerous. Tim and Pam were twins who liked to play with toys. They had many toys, but their favorite ones were the stuffed animals. They had a big bear, a small rabbit, a yellow duck, and a pink pig. They hugged them, kissed them, and talked to them every day.

One day, they saw a big truck outside their house. The truck had a sign that said "Toy Factory". Tim and Pam were curious and ran to the truck. They saw a man who was loading boxes of toys into the truck.

"Hello, mister," Tim said. "What are you doing?"

"Hello, kids," the man said. "I'm taking these toys to the toy factory. They are old and broken, and we need to make new ones."

"Can we see the toys?" Pam asked.

"Sure, why not?" the man said. "But be careful, some of them are sharp and dirty."

The man opened a box and showed them the toys. Tim and Pam saw dolls, cars, trains, and robots. But they did not look like their toys. They were missing eyes, arms, legs, and wheels. They were torn, scratched, and stained. They did not look happy or fun.

"These toys are sad," Tim said.

"These toys are ugly," Pam said.

The man laughed. "They are not sad or ugly, they are just old and broken. They don't fit in the toy store anymore. They need to go to the toy factory, where we will melt them, cut them, and glue them into new toys. Then they will fit in the toy store again."

Tim and Pam did not like the sound of that. They thought of their stuffed animals, who were soft and warm and friendly. They did not want them to go to the toy factory, where they would be melted, cut, and glued. They wanted them to stay with them, where they would be loved and cared for.

"Can we take some of these toys home?" Tim asked.

"No, you can't," the man said. "These toys belong to the toy factory. You can't have them."

"But they need a home," Pam said.

"They have a home, the toy factory. Now go away, kids. I have to finish my work."

The man closed the box and pushed them away. Tim and Pam were sad and angry. They decided to do something. They waited until the man was busy with another box, and then they ran to the truck. They climbed inside and looked for their stuffed animals. They found them in a big bag, along with other stuffed animals. They grabbed them and tried to get out of the truck.

But they were too late. The man saw them and shouted. He ran to the truck and locked the door. He said, "You naughty kids, you can't steal my toys. You have to go to the toy factory with them. Maybe they will make you into new toys too."

Tim and Pam were scared and sorry. They hugged their stuffed animals and cried. They wished they had listened to their mom, who told them not to talk to strangers or go near the truck. They wished they had stayed at home, where they were safe and happy. They learned a hard lesson: don't be greedy or curious, or you might end up in trouble.

At the store, Lily saw many things that she liked. She saw books, candy, and stickers. She wanted to have them all. She asked her mom, "Can I have these, please?" Her mom said, "No, Lily, you can't have everything. You have to pay for them. And you have too many toys already. You should be happy with what you have."

Lily was not happy. She was angry and sad. She did not listen to her mom. She put some candy and stickers in her pocket when her mom was not looking. She thought, "I don't have to pay for them. They are mine now."

But when they were leaving the store, a man stopped them. He was the store owner. He said, "Excuse me, miss, I think your daughter took something from my store without paying. Can I check her pocket?" Lily's mom was shocked and ashamed. She said, "Lily, is this true? Did you steal something?" Lily felt scared and guilty. She nodded and took out the candy and stickers from her pocket. She said, "I'm sorry, mom. I'm sorry, sir. I was wrong. I should have paid for them."

The store owner was kind and forgiving. He said, "I'm glad you are sorry, Lily. But you have to learn that stealing is bad. You have to pay for what you want. And you have to respect other people's things. Do you understand?" Lily said, "Yes, sir. I understand. I will never steal again." The store owner said, "That's good. Here, you can have one candy and one sticker as a gift. But you have to share them with someone else. Can you do that?" Lily said, "Yes, sir. I can do that. Thank you."

Lily and her mom went home. Lily felt sorry for what she did. She also felt happy for what she got. She decided to share her candy and sticker with her neighbor, Ben. The moral of the story is: Stealing is bad and sharing is good. Paying for what you want is fair and respectful. Making friends is fun and easy. Being shy is not a problem if you are kind and honest.

When they finally arrived at the top, Timmy saw the most beautiful view he had ever seen. He turned to his mom and said, "Wow, this is amazing!"

Later that day, they went on a hike. Timmy's mom warned him to be careful because the ground was rocky and he could trip. Timmy was careful, but he still tripped and fell. He hurt his knee and started to cry. His dad picked him up and said, "Don't worry, we'll take care of you." They put a bandage on his knee and Timmy felt better.

As they walked back to the car, Timmy looked up at the mountain and said, "I love to travel, but I'm glad we're going home now." His mom smiled and said, "Me too, Timmy. Me too."

The blueberry kept climbing, feeling inspired by the cheering. Eventually it made it to the end of the branch and shouted out a big thank you to all the other blueberries. The blueberries cheered even louder and applauded even more. 

The blueberry felt so proud and so brave. Now it could face anything thanks to the encouragement of its friends. The blueberry felt safe and secure, and each time it looked up at the sky, it was reminded of the courage it had found within itself.

Once upon a time, there was a little fish. He had a hook that he loved very much. All day long he played with it in the open water. 

One day, the fish decided he wanted to take his hook and go on an adventure. He packed up his hook, and swam away from home. 

The fish swam and swam, until he found a nice, open, sunny spot. He thought it was the perfect place for an adventure, and he unpacked his hook and began to play.

But then a big, scary fish came along. He saw the little fish and wanted the hook for himself. He chased after the little fish and snatched the hook away. The little fish was so scared that he swam as fast as he could, and he never saw his hook again.

The moral of the story is: never pack up and leave home unless you know the area is safe.

She was happy. She had a big and shiny corn now.
