Lily was a wealthy girl who had many toys and clothes. She liked to play with her dolls and dress them up. She did not like to share or be nice to others. She thought she was better than everyone.

One day, she went to visit her uncle, who worked in a lab. He was a scientist who studied animals and plants. He showed her some of his experiments and told her to be careful and not touch anything. Lily did not listen. She was bored and curious.

She saw a big glass jar with a frog inside. The frog was green and had red spots. It looked funny and ugly. Lily wanted to see it closer. She opened the jar and took out the frog. She stared at it and laughed. She squeezed it and pulled its legs. The frog was scared and hurt.

The frog did not like Lily. It was a special frog that had a secret. It could spit fire when it was angry. The frog opened its mouth and spat fire at Lily. The fire burned Lily's face and hair. Lily screamed and dropped the frog. The fire spread to the lab and set everything on fire. Lily and her uncle ran out of the lab, but they were too late. The fire was too big and fast. The lab exploded and the frog died.

Lily was very sad and sorry. She had lost her uncle, his lab, and his experiments. She had also lost her beauty and her toys and clothes. She had to go to the hospital and get bandages and medicine. She had no friends and no fun. She learned a hard lesson. She should have been careful and kind.

Lily was nervous. She had to go to a new school today. She did not know any of the other kids or the teacher. She wanted to stay at home with her mom and dad and play with her toys.

But mom and dad said she had to go. They said school was fun and she would learn many new things. They said they would pick her up later and give her a big hug. They said they were proud of her.

Lily got in the car with her backpack and her lunch box. She waved goodbye to mom and dad and tried to be brave. She got to the school and followed the signs to her classroom. She saw a lot of kids sitting in chairs and a lady with a smile.

The lady said, "Hello, I'm Miss Rose. You must be Lily. Welcome to our class. We are happy to have you here. Why don't you find a seat and make a friend?"

Lily looked around and saw a boy with glasses and a red shirt. He had a big book on his desk. He looked nice. Lily walked over to him and said, "Hi, I'm Lily. What's your name?"

The boy said, "Hi, I'm Ben. I like your backpack. It has stars on it. Do you like stars?"

Lily said, "Yes, I do. I like to look at them at night. They are shiny and pretty."

Ben said, "Me too. I also like to look at things that are very small. Like bugs and leaves and sand. Do you want to see something cool?"

Lily said, "Sure, what is it?"

Ben said, "It's a microscope. It makes things look bigger. You can see things you can't see with your eyes. Do you want to try it?"

Lily said, "Yes, please. How do you use it?"

Ben said, "You put something on this slide and then you look through this hole. You can turn this knob to make it clearer. Here, I have a feather. Let's look at it."

Lily put the feather on the slide and looked through the hole. She gasped. She saw many tiny hairs and colors and patterns. She said, "Wow, it's amazing. It's like a rainbow. I never knew feathers were like that."

Ben said, "I know, right? It's fun to learn new things. Do you want to see something else?"

Lily said, "Yes, please. What else do you have?"

Ben said, "I have a leaf, a coin, a hair, and a sugar cube. Which one do you want to see?"

Lily said, "Let's see the sugar cube. I like sugar. It's sweet."

Ben said, "Okay, let's see the sugar cube. Maybe we can see the crystals."

They put the sugar cube on the slide and looked through the hole. They saw many tiny squares and sparkles. They said, "Wow, it's beautiful. It's like a treasure."

They smiled at each other and became friends. They learned a lot from the microscope. They also learned that school was not so scary after all. They had fun and they were happy.

Tim and Lily are friends. They like to play in the park. They enjoy the swings, the slide and the sandbox. They also like to talk to the old man who sits on the bench. He is kind and tells them stories.

One day, the sky is grey and the wind is harsh. Tim and Lily are sad. They cannot go to the park. They stay at home and look out the window. They miss the old man and his stories.

They hear a knock on the door. They run to open it. They see the old man with a big smile. He has a bag in his hand. He says, "Hello, Tim and Lily. I have a surprise for you. Do you want to see?"

Tim and Lily nod and invite him in. They sit on the couch and the old man opens his bag. He takes out a book with colorful pictures. He says, "This is a book of fairy tales. I used to read it to my children when they were little. Now I want to read it to you. Do you like fairy tales?"

Tim and Lily clap and say, "Yes, we do. We love fairy tales. Thank you, old man. You are very nice."

The old man smiles and says, "You are very welcome, Tim and Lily. You are very sweet. Now, let's begin. Once upon a time..."

Tim and Lily were twins who liked to play in the garden. One day, they found a shiny rock that looked like gold. They both wanted to keep it for themselves.

"Give me the gold, it's mine!" Tim said.

"No, it's mine, I saw it first!" Lily said.

They pulled and pushed and shouted at each other. They did not share or say sorry. Their mom heard the noise and came to see what was wrong.

"What are you doing, Tim and Lily? Why are you fighting?" Mom asked.

They both told her their side of the story. Mom looked at the rock and shook her head.

"This is not gold, it's just a rock. It's not worth fighting over. You should share and be kind to each other. Fighting is not nice. It makes you and others sad." Mom said.

She took the rock and put it back in the garden. She told Tim and Lily to hug and say sorry. They did as she said. They felt bad for being harsh to each other.

"Sorry, Tim. You can have the rock if you want." Lily said.

"Sorry, Lily. You can have it too. We can take turns." Tim said.

They hugged and smiled. They decided to play something else in the garden. They settled their fight and were happy again. Mom was proud of them. She gave them a kiss and a cookie. They thanked her and shared the cookie. They learned a lesson that day. Sharing is caring.

Sam and Ben are friends. They like to play with cars. They have many cars of different colors and sizes. They make a row of cars on the floor. They pretend the cars are racing.

"Look, my red car is the fastest!" Sam says.

"No, my blue car is the fastest!" Ben says.

They push their cars along the row. They make noises like vroom and beep. They have fun.

But then, Sam sees a yellow car. He likes the yellow car. He wants to play with it. He reaches for the yellow car. But the yellow car belongs to Ben.

"Hey, that's my car!" Ben says. He pulls the yellow car away from Sam.

"Give it to me!" Sam says. He tries to grab the yellow car back.

They tug and pull on the yellow car. They get angry. They forget to be nice.

The yellow car breaks. It snaps in half. Sam and Ben stop. They look at the broken car. They feel sad. They feel hurt.

"I'm sorry, Ben," Sam says. "I didn't mean to break your car."

"I'm sorry, Sam," Ben says. "I didn't mean to be mean to you."

They hug. They say they are still friends. They share their cars. They play together again. They are happy.

Ben and Lily were playing in the park. They saw a big net on the grass. They wanted to catch some bugs with it.

"Look, a net!" Ben said. "Let's catch some bugs!"

"Okay!" Lily said. "But we have to be careful. The net is not ours. Maybe someone left it here."

They ran to the net and picked it up. They saw a lot of bugs flying and crawling around. They tried to catch them with the net.

"Got one!" Ben said. He caught a butterfly in the net. He was happy.

"Me too!" Lily said. She caught a ladybug in the net. She was happy too.

They put the bugs in a jar. They wanted to keep them as pets.

But then they heard a voice. It was a boy. He was looking for his net.

"Hey, that's my net!" the boy said. "You took my net!"

Ben and Lily felt scared. They did not know what to do.

"Sorry, we did not know it was yours," Ben said. "We just wanted to catch some bugs."

"Well, you can't do that," the boy said. "The net is mine. I left it here for a minute. You have to give it back."

Ben and Lily looked at each other. They liked the net and the bugs. But they knew it was wrong to take something that was not theirs.

They decided to be honest. They gave the net and the jar back to the boy.

"Here, take your net and your bugs," Lily said. "We are sorry we took them."

The boy took the net and the jar. He looked at Ben and Lily. He saw that they were sorry. He decided to be kind.

"Thank you for being honest," the boy said. "You can keep one bug each. I have enough. Do you want to be my friends?"

Ben and Lily smiled. They accepted the boy's offer. They each chose a bug to keep. They thanked the boy.

They became friends. They played with the net and the bugs together. They learned to share and to be honest.

The end.

Tim and Sam were friends who liked to play with toys. They had many toys, but their favorite was a pistol that made loud noises and flashed lights. They pretended to be cowboys and robbers with the pistol.

One day, they went to the park with their moms. They saw a big slide and wanted to go on it. They ran to the slide, but there was a boy who was bigger than them. He said, "This is my slide. You can't play here."

Tim and Sam were scared of the boy. They tried to be nice and said, "Can we play with you? We have a pistol. We can include you in our game."

The boy looked at their pistol and laughed. He said, "That's not a real pistol. That's a toy. It's disgusting. You are babies. Go away."

He grabbed the pistol from Tim's hand and threw it on the ground. He stomped on it with his foot. The pistol broke into pieces. It made no more noises and flashed no more lights.

Tim and Sam cried. They ran to their moms and told them what happened. Their moms hugged them and said, "We're sorry. That boy was very mean. He shouldn't have done that. We'll get you a new pistol."

But Tim and Sam were very sad. They loved their pistol. It was their favorite toy. They didn't want a new one. They wanted their old one. They felt like they lost a friend. They never played with the boy again.

Tom and Lily were playing with their crayons. They liked to draw different things with different colors. Tom drew a big sun with yellow. Lily drew a pretty flower with pink. They were happy.

But then, Tom saw Lily's pink crayon. He wanted it. He was greedy. He took it from her hand when she was not looking. He hid it behind his back. Lily looked for her pink crayon. She could not find it. She was sad.

"Tom, where is my pink crayon?" she asked. "I need it for my flower."

Tom lied. He said, "I don't know. Maybe it disappeared."

Lily did not believe him. She saw a little bit of pink behind his back. She was angry. She said, "No, you have it. Give it back to me. It is mine."

Tom did not want to give it back. He said, "No, it is mine now. I like pink. Go away."

Lily tried to grab the pink crayon from Tom. Tom pushed her away. They fought. They yelled. They cried. They were not happy.

Their mom heard the noise. She came to see what was wrong. She saw Tom and Lily fighting over the pink crayon. She was disappointed. She said, "Stop it, both of you. You are not nice. You are not sharing. You are not friends. You make me sad."

She took the pink crayon from Tom. She gave it back to Lily. She said, "Lily, you can have your pink crayon. It is yours. Tom, you can not have it. It is not yours. You were wrong. You were mean. You have to say sorry."

Tom did not want to say sorry. He was stubborn. He said, "No, I don't want to say sorry. I don't care. I don't like Lily. I don't like pink. I don't like you."

He ran away. He went to his room. He slammed the door. He was alone. He was hungry. He had no crayons. He had no friends. He had no fun. He was not happy. He was sorry. But it was too late. He disappeared.

Lily looked for Ben in the living room, the kitchen, the bedroom, but she could not see him. She was getting upset. She wanted to find Ben and have fun. Lily was not happy. She was angry and sad. She did not like Ben's trick. She thought he was mean. She started to cry.

"I'm sorry, Lily," he said. "I was just playing. You are a good seeker. You are my friend."

"It's okay, Ben," she said. "I was just upset. You are a good hider. You are my friend."

But then, something scary happens. The lights go out and the room becomes dark. Tim and Mia cannot see anything. They hear a loud noise and a flash. They think it is thunder and lightning. They are afraid of thunder and lightning. They hold each other's hands and try to find their teacher.

"Teacher, teacher, where are you?" they cry.

"I'm here, don't worry, it's just a power cut," the teacher says. "The lights will come back soon. Stay calm and stay in the circle."

But Tim and Mia do not hear the teacher. They panic. They run to the door and try to open it. But the door is locked. They bang on the door and scream for help.

"Help, help, let us out!" they shout.

Suddenly, the door opens and a man comes in. He has a large flashlight and a large hat. He looks at Tim and Mia and smiles.

"Hello, I'm the janitor. I came to fix the power. Are you OK?" he asks.

Tim and Mia are not OK. They are very scared. They think the man is a monster. They see his large flashlight and his large hat and his large eyes. They scream louder and hide behind a table.

"Please, don't hurt us, go away!" they beg.

The man is confused. He is not a monster. He is a nice man. He wants to help Tim and Mia. He puts down his flashlight and his hat and kneels down.

"I'm sorry, I didn't mean to scare you. I'm not a monster. I'm a friend. See, I have a badge with my name. It says Bob. Can you say Bob?" he says.

Tim and Mia peek from behind the table. They see the man's badge and his face. He does not look like a monster. He looks like a person. They say his name.

"Bob," they say.

"That's right, Bob. And what are your names?" he asks.

"Tim," says Tim.

"Mia," says Mia.

"Nice to meet you, Tim and Mia. You are very brave pupils. You know what? The power is back on. The lights are on. Do you want to go back to your teacher and your friends?" he says.

Tim and Mia look around. They see the lights are on. They see their teacher and their friends in the circle. They see their blocks and their pictures. They feel better. They nod.

"Yes, please," they say.

Bob helps them up and leads them to the circle. He gives them a high five and a hug. He says goodbye and leaves. Tim and Mia join their teacher and their friends. They listen to the story. They are happy. They are not afraid of thunder and lightning anymore. They are not afraid of Bob anymore. They are best friends.

One day, they play match on the floor of their room. They spread all the cards face down. Then they take turns to flip two cards and see if they match. If they match, they keep them. If they don't, they put them back.

"Look, I found two cards with apples!" Lily says. She shows Ben her cards. They are both red and round.

"Can we play match again tomorrow?" Ben asks.

"No, it is not lemon. One more guess."

They flew for a long time, until they saw a cave. It was dark and cold, but it was big enough for Max. He landed and let Lily down. He said, "This is my new home. Do you like it?"

Lily looked around and said, "It's nice, Max. But it's not as nice as you. I will miss you, Max. Can I come back to see you?"

Max smiled and said, "Of course, Lily. You can come back anytime. I will always be here for you. You are my best friend. And you are the one who made me grow."

They hugged and said goodbye. Lily walked back to the garden, where her parents were waiting for her. They were worried and angry, but they were also amazed and proud. They saw what Lily had done, and they knew she was special.

Lily told them everything, and they listened and hugged her. They said, "We love you, Lily. And we are happy for you and Max. But you have to be careful. Not everyone will understand. Not everyone will be kind. You have to keep this a secret. Can you do that?"

Lily nodded and said, "I can do that. I can keep a secret. But I can also grow. And I can also be free. Just like Max."

The end.

Sara loved yogurt. She ate it every morning with her spoon. She liked all kinds of yogurt: plain, strawberry, banana, peach. But today, she had a problem. Her mom gave her a new yogurt that she had never seen before. It was green and had bits of something in it.

"What is this, mom?" Sara asked, looking at the yogurt with a troubled face.

"It's kiwi yogurt, Sara. It's very yummy and healthy. Try it, you might like it," her mom said, smiling.

Sara took a small bite of the yogurt. She did not like it at all. It was sour and bitter and had seeds that got stuck in her teeth. She made a face and spit it out.

"Yuck! I don't like this yogurt, mom. It's bad. I want a different yogurt," Sara complained, pushing the bowl away.

"Come on, Sara, don't be so picky. You have to eat something for breakfast. You can't waste food. Give it another chance, maybe it will grow on you," her mom said, trying to be patient.

"No, no, no! I don't want this yogurt. I want strawberry yogurt. Strawberry yogurt is good. This yogurt is icky. Please, mom, please, can I have strawberry yogurt?" Sara begged, making a sad face.

Her mom sighed. She knew Sara was a fussy eater, but she also wanted her to try new things and not be wasteful. She decided to make a deal with her.

"Okay, Sara, how about this: if you eat half of this yogurt, I will give you a small cup of strawberry yogurt as a treat. But you have to eat at least half, no less. Deal?" her mom said, holding out her hand.

Sara thought about it. She really wanted strawberry yogurt, but she also really hated kiwi yogurt. She looked at the green bowl and then at her mom's hand. She decided to take the deal.

"Deal," she said, shaking her mom's hand.

She picked up her spoon and ate the yogurt as fast as she could, making faces and noises. She tried not to taste it too much. She counted the bites in her head. One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight. She was done. She showed her mom the empty half of the bowl.

"See, mom, I ate half. Can I have strawberry yogurt now?" she asked, hoping her mom would keep her promise.

Her mom smiled and nodded. She was proud of Sara for trying something new, even if she didn't like it. She got a small cup of strawberry yogurt from the fridge and gave it to Sara.

"Here you go, Sara. You earned it. Good job, sweetie," she said, kissing her on the cheek.

Sara smiled and thanked her mom. She opened the cup and ate the strawberry yogurt with delight. It was sweet and creamy and had no seeds. She liked it a lot. She decided that maybe trying new things was not so bad, as long as she got her favorite yogurt afterwards.

Joe kept chasing Jane around the park. They were both getting tired and still, Joe wouldn't stop. Finally, Jane got away and hid behind a tall tree. She was so scared she started to cry. Joe shouted her name over and over again, but Jane would not come out.

Eventually, Joe gave up and went home. All day Jane stayed behind that tree, too scared to come out. Poor Jane was so scared, she never did go back to the park again.

Dory had an idea. "Let's ask the wise old turtle. He knows everything about staying healthy in the ocean," she said. So, they swam to the wise old turtle's cave and asked him for advice. The turtle told Nemo to eat healthy food and exercise every day to prevent getting sick.

Nemo followed the turtle's advice and soon felt better. He was able to swim and play with his friends again, feeling normal once more. "Thank you, wise old turtle!" Nemo said happily.

The next morning, Timmy woke up and ran to the kitchen to get his milk. But when he got there, he saw something strange. There was a bald man in his kitchen! Timmy was scared at first, but then he realized it was just his dad. 

Timmy's dad explained to him that sometimes people lose their hair when they get older. Timmy didn't like the idea of losing his hair, but he was happy to know that his dad was still the same person, even without his hair. And he was even happier to drink his milk and start his day.

Sam and Mia were friends who liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a big melon on a table. It was green and round and looked yummy.

"Let's share the melon," Sam said.

"OK," Mia agreed.

They went to the table and tried to cut the melon with a plastic knife. But the melon was too hard and the knife was too soft. They could not cut it.

"Let me try," Sam said. He pushed Mia away and took the knife.

"No, let me try," Mia said. She pulled Sam back and grabbed the knife.

They started to fight over the knife and the melon. They pulled and pushed and shouted.

"Stop!" a voice said. It was the owner of the melon. He was a man with a hat and a beard. He looked angry.

"What are you doing with my melon?" he asked.

Sam and Mia stopped fighting. They felt scared and sorry.

"We wanted to share the melon," Sam said.

"We did not know it was yours," Mia said.

The man sighed. He saw that they were just kids who were hungry and curious.

"Well, it is my melon, but I can share it with you," he said. "But you have to promise me something."

"What?" Sam and Mia asked.

"You have to promise me that you will not fight over things that are not yours. And you have to promise me that you will be original and creative. You can make up your own stories and games and toys. You don't need a melon to have fun."

Sam and Mia nodded. They promised the man. They thanked him for the melon. He cut it for them and gave them each a slice. It was sweet and juicy.

They ate the melon and smiled. They decided to be friends again. They also decided to be original and creative. They used the melon rinds as hats and pretended to be pirates. They had fun in the park.

"Look, I found a big bug!" Tom said, holding a worm in his hand.

"Yuck, that is a filthy bug!" Amy said, making a face. "Put it back in the sand!"

Tom did not want to put the bug back. He wanted to keep it as a pet. He put the bug in his pocket and said, "No, I like this bug. He is my friend. I will call him Wiggly."

Amy shrugged and kept digging. She hoped to find something better than a bug. She dug deeper and deeper, until she hit something hard. She pulled it out and saw that it was a shiny coin.

"Wow, I found a coin!" Amy said, showing it to Tom. "This is a good result!"

Tom nodded and hugged Amy back. He said, "Thank you, Amy. You are a good friend. I am sorry I was mean to you."

Amy smiled and said, "You are welcome, Tom. You are a good friend too. I am sorry I was rude to you."

Lily and Ben felt bad. They did not mean to hurt their dad's feelings. They said, "We are sorry, dad. We did not know the camera reversed. We thought it was funny, but we see it was rude. You are not ugly, dad. You are handsome and kind. We love you."

Jack got upset and took Dolly away from Lily. Lily cried and said, "Give Dolly back, she's mine!" But Jack didn't listen and threw Dolly out of the window. 

Lily was very sad and couldn't find her adorable Dolly anywhere. She cried and cried until her parents came to comfort her. They told her that sometimes people can be mean, but it's important to be kind to others. From that day on, Lily learned to share her toys with others and never let anyone take away her happiness again.

Lily was sad. She really wanted to drink the magical purple milk. "But I really believe that the purple milk can make me fly," she said. Her mom smiled and said, "Well, maybe one day we'll find some purple milk for you to try."

Lily was happy again, knowing that her mom believed in her magical purple milk too. She drank her white milk and went to play outside, dreaming of the day she could finally drink the purple milk and fly like a bird.

Tim was sad but he knew his mom was right. He picked a safe toy instead. Tim and his mom went home, and he played with his new toy all day.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Tweet. Tweet loved to fly up high in the sky and soar like a superhero. One day, Tweet was flying over a field when she saw a blueberry bush. She decided to land and have a snack.

As she was eating, Tweet noticed an unusual bug crawling on one of the blueberries. "Hello there, little bug," said Tweet. "What are you doing on this blueberry?"

"I'm just having a snack like you," replied the bug. "But this blueberry is extra special. It's the biggest and juiciest one I've ever seen!"

Tweet was curious. "Why is it so special?" she asked.

"Well," said the bug, "it's because it's been soaking up all the sunshine and rain for weeks. That's why it's so big and delicious."

Tweet was amazed. She had never thought about blueberries like that before. From that day on, she always made sure to stop by the blueberry bush whenever she was flying by.

There was a monkey who lived in a big tree. He liked to play and jump and swing on the branches. He was happy, but he was also ignorant. He did not know how to share or be kind to other animals.

One day, he saw a bird who had a shiny thing in her beak. He wanted the shiny thing for himself, so he tried to snatch it from the bird. But the bird was faster and flew away. The monkey was angry and chased the bird all over the tree.

The bird was scared and tired. She flew to a nest where her friend, a squirrel, was waiting. The squirrel saw the monkey and asked him, "Why are you bothering the bird? She did nothing wrong to you."

The monkey said, "I want her shiny thing. It is mine."

The squirrel said, "No, it is not yours. It is hers. She found it in the grass. It is a ring. It belonged to a human who lost it. You cannot have it. You are being greedy and rude."

The monkey did not listen. He tried to climb to the nest and grab the ring. But the squirrel was clever and brave. He threw a nut at the monkey's head and made him fall. The monkey landed on the ground with a thud. He hurt his tail and his pride.

He looked up and saw the bird and the squirrel laughing at him. He felt ashamed and sorry. He realized he was wrong and ignorant. He learned his lesson. He said, "I am sorry, bird and squirrel. I was foolish and mean. I do not want your shiny thing anymore. Can you forgive me?"

The bird and the squirrel saw that the monkey was sincere and humble. They said, "We forgive you, monkey. But you have to promise to be nice and share from now on."

The monkey nodded and smiled. He said, "I promise. Thank you for teaching me. Can we be friends?"

The bird and the squirrel agreed. They invited the monkey to join them in their nest. They shared the ring and some nuts and berries. They played and talked and had fun. The monkey was happy and wise. He never tried to take what was not his again.

The moral of the story is: Do not be ignorant and greedy. Be kind and share. You will make more friends and be happier.

The plant King said, "If you ever come here again, I'll turn you into a plant!"

The silly bear ran out of the forest as quickly as he could and never came back.

Once upon a time, there was a nice duck who enjoyed playing in the mud. He liked to get his feathers all mucky so he could be brown like the others.

But one day, the duck realized the mud was extra hot. He started to panic, since he didn't know why it was so hot. He tried to fly away, but the mud was melted together! He had gotten himself stuck!

The duck started to quack in fear. But then he remembered an old story he had heard from his parents about the sun burning the mud. And that's the exact what happened! The sun had made the mud too hot and the duck was stuck in the mud.

The duck tried to flap its wings, but he was stuck too tight. Just then, he heard a friendly voice. It was the farmer, who had seen the nice duck get stuck. He came to help and slowly pulled the duck out of the mud.

The farmer was so nice and the duck was always thankful that he had come. The farmer even gave the duck a bath afterwards so he wasn't all mucky anymore. From that day forward, the duck was extra careful; he only played in the mud when the sun wasn't too hot.

John spent the whole day playing with his car, driving it up and down the driveway and onto the front lawn. Suddenly, the knob started to move and he felt something snap inside the car. John was scared, but he was determined to fix it.

He went inside to ask his dad for help. As his dad reached for the knob, he warned John to be careful. He could feel the tension in the knob and knew something was about to happen.

Suddenly, the knob popped off and a loud sound filled the air. John was so fearful, he ran away and hid under the kitchen table. His dad popped the knob back on and fixed the car.

John was so relieved that his car was back to normal. He would always remember this day, and be extra careful when playing with things that have knobs.

Sue and Kitty looked for rocks every day. They found many rocks and sold them to their friends. Soon, they had enough money to buy a new toy. Sue and Kitty were very happy and played with their new toy all day long.

Once upon a time, there was a little sunflower named Sunny. Sunny lived in a big garden with many other flowers. But Sunny was sad because she thought she was ugly. All the other flowers were very pretty and did not want to play with her.

One day, a kind girl named Lucy came to the garden. Lucy saw Sunny and thought she was special. Lucy wanted to help Sunny. So, she asked her mom if she could take care of Sunny. Her mom said yes and allowed Lucy to take Sunny home.

Lucy took care of Sunny every day. She gave her water and lots of love. Soon, Sunny started to grow bigger and more beautiful. The other flowers saw how pretty Sunny was and wanted to play with her. But Sunny knew that true friends are kind, like Lucy, and don't care if you are ugly or pretty.

Once upon a time, there was a little fish named Fin. Fin lived in the big ocean with his family. They all swam and played together every day. Fin loved his home, but sometimes he felt uncomfortable. He thought he did not fit in with the other fish because he was smaller than them.

One day, a big storm came and made the ocean very wavy. The waves pushed all the fish far away from their home. The big fish were scared and did not know how to get back. But Fin, being small, could swim through the small spaces between the rocks and plants.

Fin found a safe path back home and showed the big fish the way. They all swam together and were happy to be home again. Fin was no longer uncomfortable because he learned that being different can be good. The other fish thanked him, and they all played together, knowing that everyone fits in, no matter their size.

Mia saw her friend Tom looking troubled. She asked, "Why are you sad, Tom?" Tom said, "I lost my toy car, and I can't find it." Mia wanted to help Tom, so they both looked for the toy car.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a lazy cat named Tom. Tom loved to sleep all day and never helped his friends.

One day, Tom's friend, a little bird named Lucy, found a secret. Lucy told Tom, "I found a magic word that can restore anything that is broken!" Tom was curious but too lazy to find out more.

Soon, there was a big storm, and many houses were broken. All the animals were sad. Lucy said to Tom, "Now is the time to use the secret word to restore the houses!" But Tom was too lazy and wanted to sleep.

The other animals heard about the secret and worked together to fix the houses. They asked Tom to help, but he still said no. The animals were upset with Tom for being so lazy.

In the end, Tom saw how hard his friends worked and felt bad. He decided to help and used the secret word to restore the last broken house. Tom learned that being lazy is not good, and it is important to help friends when they need it.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a toy car that needed a battery to make it go. One day, the toy car stopped moving. Lily was sad.

Lily's dad came and said, "Let me see the toy car." He opened the car and found a thick layer of dirt inside. "Look, Lily, the dirt is stopping the battery from working. We need to rub it clean."

Lily and her dad rubbed the dirt away from the battery. They put the battery back in the toy car, and it started moving again. Lily was happy and thanked her dad.

The moral of the story is to always keep your toys clean so they work well.

Once upon a time, there was an old octopus who lived in the ocean. He was very slow and had eight long arms. One day, he met a small fish who was swimming nearby.

"Hello, little fish," said the elderly octopus. "Do you want to play with me?"

The little fish replied, "Yes, I want to play with you. But first, can I ask you a question?"

"Of course," said the octopus.

"Why do you have so many arms?" asked the little fish.

"I use them to catch my food," replied the octopus. "I chew my food with my beak, just like a bird."

The little fish was amazed. "Wow, that's so cool!" she said.

And so, the elderly octopus and the little fish became friends and played together every day in the ocean.

Lily liked to hide. She hid under the bed, behind the sofa, in the closet. She hid from her mom, her dad, her brother. She hid when it was time to eat, time to sleep, time to play. She thought hiding was fun.

One day, Lily saw a rainbow in the sky. It was big and bright and had many colors. Lily wanted to see it closer. She ran outside and looked for a place to hide. She saw a big tree with a hole in it. She thought it was a good hiding spot.

She crawled into the hole and waited. She hoped the rainbow would come to her. She waited and waited and waited. She heard a voice. It was not her mom, her dad, or her brother. It was a small and squeaky voice.

"Hello, who are you?" the voice said. Lily was scared. She peeked out of the hole. She saw a tiny mouse with a red hat. The mouse looked at her and smiled.

"I'm Lily. Who are you?" Lily said.

"I'm Max. I live here. This is my home. Do you want to be my friend?" Max said.

Lily nodded. She liked Max. He was cute and friendly. He showed her his home. He had a bed, a table, a chair, and a book. He also had a picture of a rainbow.

"That's a rainbow. I like rainbows. Do you like rainbows?" Max said.

"Yes, I do. I came here to see the rainbow. It's in the sky. It's big and bright and has many colors." Lily said.

"Really? Can I see it too?" Max said.

"Sure. Come with me. We can go outside and see the rainbow." Lily said.

Lily and Max crawled out of the hole. They looked up at the sky. They saw the rainbow. It was still there. It was still big and bright and had many colors. Lily and Max smiled. They held hands. They were happy.

They did not know that the rainbow was famous. It was the most beautiful rainbow in the world. Many people came to see it. They took pictures and videos. They posted them on the internet. They said it was a miracle. They said it was a sign. They said it was a wonder.

But Lily and Max did not care. They only cared about each other. They were friends. They had fun. They hid under the rainbow.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big flower. It is yellow and red. It smells good.

"Wow, look at the flower!" Lily says. "It is so pretty!"

"Can we pick it?" Ben asks.

"No, we can't," Lily says. "The flower is not ours. It belongs to the park. If we pick it, it will die."

"Oh, okay," Ben says. "But can we smell it?"

"Yes, we can," Lily says. "But be gentle. Don't touch the petals."

They smell the flower. It makes them happy. They smile.

Then they hear a bell. It is time to go home. They say goodbye to the flower.

"Bye, flower," Lily says. "Thank you for being so pretty and nice."

"Bye, flower," Ben says. "Maybe we will see you again."

They run to their moms. They hold their hands. They walk away.

But Ben forgets something. He forgets his hat. He left it on the ground, next to the flower.

The flower sees the hat. It is blue and warm. It thinks the hat is a friend.

The flower is helpful. It wants to keep the hat safe. It wraps its stem around the hat. It covers it with its petals.

The next day, Lily and Ben come back to the park. They look for the flower. They want to say hello.

But they can't find it. They see a big blue ball. It is on the ground, where the flower was.

"I don't know," Ben says. "It looks like a ball. But it is not round. It has bumps."

They pull the ball. It moves. It opens. They see something inside.

It is Ben's hat!

"Hey, that's my hat!" Ben says. "I forgot it yesterday!"

He takes his hat. He puts it on his head.

He sees the flower. It is under the hat. It is still yellow and red. It is still smiling.

"Hello, flower," Ben says. "You are so helpful. You saved my hat. Thank you!"

"You're welcome," the flower says. "You are my friend. I like your hat. It is cozy."

Tim liked to sign. He learned to sign from his mom, who was deaf. He could talk with his voice, too, but he liked to use his hands. He thought it was fun and special.

One day, he went to the park with his mom and his dog, Rex. He saw a big hill with a lot of ants. He wanted to sign to the ants. He thought they might understand him. He ran to the hill and knelt down. He waved his hand and said, "Hello, ants. I am Tim. Do you want to be my friends?"

The ants did not answer. They were busy carrying food and building their home. They did not see Tim or his hand. They did not care about him. They only cared about their work.

Tim felt sad. He wanted the ants to talk to him. He tried to sign again, but louder. He said, "Please, ants. Look at me. I want to play with you. I can sign. Can you sign?"

The ants still did not answer. They still did not see Tim or his hand. They still did not care about him. They only cared about their work.

But Rex saw Tim and his hand. Rex was curious. He thought Tim was playing a game. He wanted to join the game. He ran to Tim and barked. He jumped on Tim and licked his face. He grabbed Tim's hand with his mouth and pulled.

Tim screamed. He felt pain. He dropped his hand and saw blood. Rex had bitten him. Rex did not mean to hurt him. He only wanted to play. But Tim did not know that. He was scared and angry. He pushed Rex away and cried.

Mom heard Tim and ran to him. She saw his hand and the ants and Rex. She understood what happened. She hugged Tim and said, "I'm sorry, Tim. Rex did not know you were signing. He thought you were playing. He did not want to bite you. He loves you. And the ants did not hear you. They cannot sign. They are normal ants. They do not talk. They only work. They are not your friends. They are just bugs. Come on, let's go home. I will clean your hand and give you a band-aid. And I will sign with you. I am your friend. I love you."

Tim nodded. He still felt pain and sad, but he also felt love. He hugged his mom and said, "I love you, too, mom. Thank you for signing with me. You are my best friend." He looked at Rex and said, "I love you, too, Rex. But please do not bite me again. That hurts. You are my good dog." He looked at the ants and said, "Goodbye, ants. I hope you have a good day. But I do not want to sign with you anymore. You are not my friends. You are just bugs." He got up and walked with his mom and his dog. He learned a lesson. He learned that not everyone can sign. He learned that some things are normal and some things are special. He learned that he was special. And he was happy.

Lila was a hippo who liked to be organized. She had a place for everything and everything in its place. She liked to make lists and plans and follow them every day. She was very proud of her neat and tidy home by the river.

One day, she invited her friend Milo, who was also a hippo, to come over and play. Milo was not very organized. He liked to have fun and be messy. He did not like to make lists or plans or follow them. He was always happy and curious.

When Milo arrived, he saw Lila's home and said, "Wow, you have a lot of things. Can I see them?"

Lila said, "Sure, but be careful. Don't touch anything or move anything. Everything has its place."

Milo nodded, but he did not listen. He started to look at Lila's things and touch them and move them. He found a ball and bounced it. He found a book and opened it. He found a hat and put it on. He made a lot of noise and mess.

Lila was very angry. She said, "Milo, stop it! You are ruining my things. You are making a mess. You are not being a good friend."

Milo said, "But I'm just having fun. I'm not hurting anything. I'm being a good friend. Why are you so mad?"

Lila said, "Because you are not respecting my things. You are not following my rules. You are not being organized."

Milo said, "But being organized is boring. Being fun is better. You should try it."

Lila said, "No, thank you. I like being organized. It makes me happy. You should try it."

They argued and argued. They did not listen to each other. They did not understand each other. They did not have fun.

Then, they heard a loud roar. It was a lion. He was hungry and looking for food. He saw the hippos and licked his lips.

Lila and Milo were scared. They ran to the river and jumped in. They hid under the water and hoped the lion would go away.

They stayed there for a long time. They did not talk. They did not play. They did not argue. They just rested.

After a while, they peeked out of the water. The lion was gone. They were safe.

They looked at each other and said, "I'm sorry."

Lila said, "I'm sorry for being angry. I should have let you have fun. I should have been more flexible. I should have been a better friend."

Milo said, "I'm sorry for being messy. I should have respected your things. I should have followed your rules. I should have been a better friend."

They hugged and smiled. They said, "We are different, but we are friends. We can learn from each other. We can have fun and be organized. We can be happy."

They went back to Lila's home and cleaned up the mess. They played with the ball and the book and the hat. They made a list and a plan for the next day. They had fun and were organized. They were happy.

The moral of the story is: Respect your friends and their things. Listen to them and understand them. Be flexible and adaptable. Learn from your differences. Have fun and be organized. Be happy.

There was once a boy called Tom who loved to play outside. One day, Tom found a hole in the ground. He was very curious and he wanted to see what was inside. Suddenly, he spotted something moving and saw a little caterpillar crawling around. Tom wanted to tie the little caterpillar up so he wouldn't get away.

Tom found a piece of string and he carefully tied the caterpillar's feet together. He put the caterpillar back into the hole, and filled the hole up with dirt so the caterpillar wouldn't get out. Tom felt a bit sad, but he thought the caterpillar would be safer this way.

Tom was so happy to have helped the caterpillar, but the next day, he saw that the caterpillar had died, and all that was left was a tiny cocoon. Tom remembered how bitter he had felt when he tied up the caterpillar, but he knew that it was the best thing he could do for the caterpillar. He said goodbye to the caterpillar, knowing that one day a beautiful butterfly would fly out of the hole.

The butterfly was spinning around and the duck felt a little jealous. The butterfly flew so high up in the sky that the duck could barely catch a glimpse of him.

The duck wanted to spin too, so he started to swim around in circles in the stream. The water made him twirl and spin like the butterfly. He felt so happy and free that he just kept spinning and spinning.

Soon enough, the duck's spinning made a whirlpool in the stream. The duck got so dizzy that he fell asleep. When he woke up, the butterfly was back and so was his good friend, the fish. The duck and the fish both laughed a lot and played in the stream together.

The duck never forgot the feeling of spinning in the stream, and he knew that he was much luckier than the butterfly. The butterfly never had anyone to laugh and play with. The duck was glad that he had his fish friend, and he was no longer jealous of the butterfly.

So, off they went, exploring the woods until finally, Jane spotted something very attractive. It was a big red box with blue stripes and a big gold lock on it. Jane knew right away that this was the treasure.

Her mommy smiled and said, "I promise that if you can find a way to open the lock, this will be your treasure". Jane was so happy she almost forgot to be careful. She was sure if she looked hard enough, she'd find a way to open the treasure chest.

After a few tries, Jane found a key that did the trick. When she opened the box, she squealed with delight. There were so many wonderful things inside- a toy car, a stuffed bear, and a pretty necklace. 

Jane hugged her mommy and thanked her for the promise that led her to find the treasure.

Once upon a time, there was a mighty eraser. Every day it would watch the children drawing and colouring and never felt jealous; it was happy to help them make their pictures perfect. But one day, the eraser noticed that it was being ignored. The kids were playing and talking, but they didn't even look at the eraser.

The eraser felt so sad. It tried to get the kids' attention, but they paid no mind. It waved and smiled, but they just kept playing. Finally, the eraser gave up. When the kids went home, the eraser cried; it just wanted to be useful and help the children.

Then, out of the corner of its eye, the eraser saw a butterfly. It fluttered around, reminding the eraser that it was still mighty and important. All at once, the eraser's sadness was gone. From that day on, whenever the children played the eraser would smile, knowing it still had an important job.

So, Tim smiled and started playing with the dragon. They both had lots of fun. They played until the sun started to set. Then, the dragon said goodbye and went back into the red chest. 

Tim felt sad that the dragon had to go. But, he was happy that he got to meet such a special dragon.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Joy. She had a dirty rag doll that she loved more than anything. One day, Joy was out playing in the sun when she slipped and the rag doll split in two. Joy was so sad that she quickly cried. 

Her mum came running out and said, "What's wrong my little Joy?" Joy showed her mum the dirty rag doll and said, "Look, it's split in two." 

Her mum thought for a moment and then said, "It's okay sweetheart, it's still your buddy and it will always be your friend - even if it's split in two. Things can still be special even when they're not the same anymore."

Joy thought about what her mum said, and slowly wiped away her tears. She hugged her rag doll and smiled, knowing that her buddy was still special no matter what happened. 

The moral of this story is that some things can be just as special, even if the world may not think it is.

Once upon a time there was a bear who loved to swim. The bear went to the river every day to swim and have fun, but this day something seemed very wrong. As the bear was jumping into the river, he started to shiver. He had never gotten cold before while swimming. He was so scared he quickly ran out of the river and looked around.

Then he spotted a phone on the ground. He had never seen a phone before, so he curiously poked at it with his furry paw. Suddenly, the phone started to ring! The bear was so scared he started to shiver again. 

He picked up the phone, heard a voice and was very surprised. It was a normal voice, not a scary one. The voice asked the bear if he was okay and he said yes. The voice told the bear that someone was coming to help him, so he should stay in the same spot.

Soon a nice person arrived and asked the bear if he was okay. The bear was very relieved and said yes. The nice person told the bear that the cold river water was not normal and it was making him shiver. The person took the bear with them and made sure he was warm and safe.

The bear was so relieved and thanked his lucky stars today was not a bad one.

Mia's mom said, "Mia! You scared me! Don't go anywhere without telling me first."

Mia was scared too; she had never heard her mom scream like that before. She hugged her mom tightly and said, " I'm sorry, Mom. I just wanted to see the magazine."

Mia's mom smiled and said, "It's okay, sweetie. You were just exploring. Let's go inside now, I'm very tired."

Mia put the magazine back on the ground and followed her mom inside. She knew she should always tell her mom if she wanted to explore something.

Once upon a time, there was a wise old owl who lived in a tree. He had a rubber ball that he loved to play with. One day, a little bird came to visit him. "Hello, Mr. Owl," the bird said. "Can I play with your rubber ball?"

"Sure," said the owl, "but be careful not to lose it." The little bird played with the rubber ball for a while and had a lot of fun. But then he got tired and flew away, forgetting to give the ball back to the owl.

Days went by, and the owl missed his rubber ball. He went to look for the little bird and found him in another tree. "Excuse me," said the owl, "can I have my rubber ball back?"

"I don't have it anymore," said the little bird. "I gave it to my friend."

The owl was sad because he had lost his favorite toy. The moral of the story is that we should always talk to our friends and be honest with them. If the little bird had talked to the owl and told him that he lost the rubber ball, the owl wouldn't be sad now.

"Can I play with your toy?" Ally asked the duck. 

"No, it's mine," said the duck. 

Ally was sad and went to her other friend, the turtle. "Why does the duck have a toy and not me?" Ally asked. 

The turtle replied, "The duck's owner works hard to buy him toys. Maybe you should ask your owner to work hard too." 

Ally realized the turtle was right. She went to her owner and said, "I want toys too. Can you work hard for me?" 

Her owner smiled and said, "Of course, Ally. I will work hard to buy you toys." 

From that day on, Ally learned that she could have nice things too if her owner worked hard. And she was no longer envious of her friend's toys. The end.

Ben said, "Don't be scared. It will be quick and easy. Come on, follow me."

Ben and Mia ran to the fence and jumped on it. They saw the bird and tried to catch it. But the bird was fast and flew away. Ben and Mia did not see the big car that was coming on the street. The car was loud and fast and did not stop. The car hit Ben and Mia and they fell from the fence. They were hurt and bleeding and could not move. The lady heard the noise and came to the street. She saw Ben and Mia and cried. She picked them up and took them to the home. She called the vet and tried to help them. But it was too late. Ben and Mia died.

The moral of the story is: you should obey the law and not go to dangerous places. If you do, you may get hurt or die. You should listen to your friends who warn you and care for you. You should be happy with what you have and not be greedy for what you don't.

Tom and Mia are friends. They like to play in the park. They have a big blanket. They spread the blanket on the grass. They sit on the blanket and have a picnic.

"Look, Tom, I have a lovely sandwich. Do you want some?" Mia says.

"Yes, please. I have some lovely cookies. Do you want some?" Tom says.

They share their food and smile. They are happy.

But then, a big dog comes. The dog is hungry. The dog sees the food on the blanket. The dog runs to the blanket and jumps on it. The food falls off the blanket. The dog eats the food.

"Hey, stop! That is our food!" Tom shouts.

"Go away, dog! You are bad!" Mia cries.

They try to push the dog away. But the dog is strong. The dog growls and barks. Tom and Mia are scared.

A man comes. The man is the dog's owner. The man sees the dog and the children. The man is sorry.

"I'm so sorry, kids. He is a naughty dog. He doesn't listen. Come here, boy!" The man says.

The man takes the dog away. The dog whines. The man apologizes again.

Tom and Mia look at their blanket. Their blanket is dirty. Their food is gone. They are sad.

But then, they see something. They see a wide basket. The basket is full of food. The basket has a note. The note says:

"Dear Tom and Mia, I'm very sorry for what my dog did. He is a good dog, but he has a big appetite. Please take this basket as a gift. I hope you enjoy it. Have a lovely day. From, the man and the dog."

Tom and Mia are surprised. They are happy. They thank the man and the dog. They take the basket. They spread the blanket again. They sit on the blanket and have a new picnic.

They have a lovely day.

"OK, but be careful. The water is cold and deep," her mom says.

Lily and Ben put on their swim suits. They jump into the water. They splash and kick and laugh. They have fun.

Then they see a chubby duck. The duck is yellow and brown. It has a long neck and a flat beak. It swims near them.

"Hello, duck," Lily says.

"Quack, quack," the duck says.

"Do you want to play with us?" Ben asks.

"Quack, quack," the duck says.

The duck swims with Lily and Ben. They chase each other and make bubbles. The duck is fast and smart.

Then the duck gets out of the water. It shakes its feathers. It walks to the grass. It sees some bread.

"Quack, quack," the duck says.

"Are you hungry, duck?" Lily asks.

"Quack, quack," the duck says.

Lily and Ben get out of the water too. They dry themselves with towels. They follow the duck to the grass. They see a man with a bag of bread.

"Can we feed the duck, please?" Ben asks the man.

"Sure, here you go. He likes bread," the man says.

He gives them some bread. They break it into small pieces. They throw it to the duck. The duck eats the bread. It is happy.

"Thank you, duck, for playing with us," Lily says.

"Quack, quack," the duck says.

"Look, the duck is dancing!" Ben says.

"Wow, the duck is dancing!" Lily says.

They clap their hands and laugh. They join the duck and dance too. They dance with the duck on the grass. They have more fun.

Lily was a little girl who liked to play with her dolls. She had many dolls, but her favorite was a lady doll with a blue dress and a big hat. She called her doll Ann and pretended she was an important lady who went to parties and meetings.

One day, Lily's mom had to go to the store and asked Lily to stay with her dad. Lily said yes and took Ann to the living room. She put Ann on the couch and said, "You stay here, Ann. I will be back soon. Don't go anywhere."

Lily went to the kitchen to get a snack. She saw a big cookie on the table and reached for it. But she did not see the button on the wall that said "shrink". She accidentally pushed the button with her elbow and heard a loud beep.

She turned around and saw a bright light coming from the living room. She ran to see what happened and gasped. The couch was gone and so was Ann. Instead, there was a tiny couch and a tiny doll on the floor. Lily had shrunk them with the button.

She picked up the tiny doll and said, "Oh no, Ann! What did I do? You are so small now. I'm sorry, I'm sorry." She hugged the doll and cried.

She heard her dad coming from upstairs. He saw Lily crying and asked, "What's wrong, Lily? What happened?"

Lily showed him the tiny doll and said, "Daddy, I shrunk Ann. She was my important lady doll. Now she is so small. Can you make her big again?"

Her dad looked at the button and the light and realized what had happened. He smiled and said, "Don't worry, Lily. It's okay. This is a special button that can shrink and grow things. It's for a science project I'm working on. Watch this."

He pushed the button again and the light flashed. The couch and the doll grew back to their normal size. Lily was amazed and happy. She hugged Ann and said, "Yay, Ann! You are big again. You are still my important lady doll. I love you."

Her dad hugged her and said, "I love you too, Lily. You are my important little girl. But please don't touch the button again. It's not a toy. It's very dangerous."

Lily nodded and said, "Okay, daddy. I won't touch the button again. I'm sorry. Can we have a cookie now?"

Her dad laughed and said, "Sure, Lily. Let's have a cookie. And maybe we can play with Ann together. She looks like a fun doll."

Lily smiled and said, "Yes, daddy. She is a fun doll. And you are a fun daddy. Thank you for making her big again."

They went to the kitchen and had a cookie. Lily and Ann were happy. They had a big adventure. But they did not want to shrink again.

Tim and Mia liked to play in the park. They liked to run, jump, and swing. They also liked to number the trees. They wanted to know how many trees there were in the park.

One day, they saw a big oak tree. It was taller and wider than the other trees. It had many leaves and acorns. Tim and Mia ran to the oak tree and touched its bark.

"Wow, this is a big tree!" Tim said. "Let's number it."

"Okay," Mia said. "How do we number it?"

Tim thought for a moment. He had an idea. He took a stick and made a mark on the ground. "This is one," he said. "Now we need to make more marks for the other trees."

Mia nodded. She took another stick and made another mark next to Tim's. "This is two," she said. "Let's go find more trees."

They ran to the next tree and made another mark. They did the same for the next tree, and the next, and the next. They had fun numbering the trees.

But then, they heard a loud roar. They turned around and saw a wild lion. It had escaped from the zoo. It was hungry and angry. It saw Tim and Mia and ran towards them.

"Run!" Tim shouted. "Run to the oak tree!"

Tim and Mia dropped their sticks and ran as fast as they could. They reached the oak tree and climbed up its branches. They hid behind the leaves and hoped the lion would not find them.

The lion came to the oak tree and sniffed around. It saw the marks on the ground. It was confused. It did not know what they meant. It roared again and tried to scratch the bark. But the oak tree was strong and did not break.

Tim and Mia were scared. They hugged each other and whispered. "What do we do?" Mia asked.

"We wait," Tim said. "We wait for help."

They waited and waited. They heard sirens and voices. They looked down and saw people and cars. They saw the zookeepers and the police. They saw them catch the lion and put it in a cage. They saw them wave at them and tell them to come down.

Tim and Mia climbed down the oak tree. They were safe and happy. They thanked the people and hugged their parents. They told them what happened and how they numbered the trees.

The people and the parents were amazed and proud. They praised Tim and Mia for being brave and smart. They gave them ice cream and stickers. They told them they could come back to the park anytime.

Tim and Mia smiled and nodded. They liked the park. They liked the oak tree. They liked to number the trees. But they did not like the wild lion. They hoped it would stay in the zoo. They hoped they would never see it again.

One day, a little girl named Mia saw a beautiful butterfly in the garden. She wanted to catch it and play with it, so she ran after it with a net. But the butterfly was very fast and smart, and it flew away from Mia every time she got close.

"Come here, butterfly!" Mia shouted. "I just want to be your friend!"

The butterfly did not listen. It did not want to be caught by Mia. It liked to be free and fly around the flowers. It saw a big rose and set on it to rest.

Mia saw the butterfly set on the rose and smiled. She thought she could catch it now. She tiptoed towards the rose and raised her net. But just as she was about to swing it, the butterfly flew away again. It was very persistent and did not give up.

Mia was very sad and angry. She threw her net on the ground and stomped her feet. She started to cry.

"Why are you crying, Mia?" her mother asked. She came out of the house and saw Mia and the net.

"I want to catch the butterfly, but it won't let me!" Mia sobbed.

Her mother hugged her and said, "Mia, you can't catch the butterfly. It is not a toy. It is a living thing that has feelings and needs. It wants to be free and happy, not trapped and scared. How would you feel if someone tried to catch you and put you in a cage?"

Mia thought about it and said, "I would feel very bad. I would miss my family and friends and the things I like to do."

"Exactly," her mother said. "So you should respect the butterfly and let it be. Maybe if you are gentle and kind, it will come to you and let you see it up close. But you can't force it to do what you want. You have to be patient and understanding."

Mia nodded and said, "I'm sorry, butterfly. I didn't mean to hurt you. I just wanted to be your friend. Can you forgive me?"

She wiped her tears and looked at the sky. She saw the butterfly flying above her. It seemed to hear her and came down to her. It set on her shoulder and fluttered its wings. Mia smiled and said, "Hello, butterfly. You are very beautiful. Thank you for coming to me."

The butterfly stayed with Mia for a while, then flew away again. Mia waved goodbye and said, "Bye, butterfly. Have a nice day. I hope to see you again."

Her mother smiled and said, "You see, Mia? Sometimes the best way to make a friend is to let them be themselves. You did a good job, Mia. I'm proud of you."

Mia hugged her mother and said, "Thank you, Mom. I love you. And I love the butterfly, too."

The end.

Lily and Ben were playing with dough in the kitchen. They liked to make shapes and pretend they were food. Lily made a dough pizza and Ben made a dough cake.

"Look at my pizza!" Lily said. "It has cheese and pepperoni and olives."

"Wow, that looks yummy!" Ben said. "And look at my cake! It has frosting and sprinkles and candles."

They put their dough creations on a tray and pretended to bake them in the oven. They set a timer and waited for their food to be ready.

Ding! The timer went off and they opened the oven. But something was wrong. Their dough was not dough anymore. It was hard and brown and smelled bad.

"What happened?" Lily asked. "Our food is ruined!"

Ben touched the dough and felt how hot and hard it was. He realized that they had made a mistake. They had used real dough, not play dough. Real dough changes when it gets hot. Play dough stays the same.

"Oh no!" Ben said. "We used the wrong dough! Mom will be so mad!"

They felt helpless. They did not know how to fix their mess. They looked at each other and started to cry.

Mom heard their cries and came to the kitchen. She saw the tray of burnt dough and smelled the smoke. She realized what had happened and felt sorry for them.

"Oh, you poor things!" she said. "You used real dough instead of play dough. That's why it turned out like this. It's okay, it was an accident. Don't cry."

She hugged them and kissed them and threw away the bad dough. She gave them some play dough and some cookies and helped them make new shapes and pretend food.

"See?" she said. "This is play dough. It's soft and colorful and fun. You can make anything you want with it. And this is real dough. It's sticky and white and boring. You can only make bread with it. Do you understand the difference?"

Lily and Ben nodded and smiled. They understood and felt better. They thanked Mom and played with their play dough and ate their cookies. They learned a lesson and had fun.

One day, Sara saw a pretty ornament in the store. It was a star with many colors. She wanted to buy it for her mom and dad, to put on their tree. She asked her mom if she could have some money. Her mom said yes, but only if she did her chores first.

Sara did her chores very fast. She cleaned her room, fed the cat, and helped with the dishes. Then she ran to the store with her money. She looked for the star ornament, but she could not find it. She asked a lady who worked there. The lady said, "I'm sorry, we sold the last one. Maybe you can find another ornament you like."

Sara felt sad. She wanted the star ornament for her mom and dad. She looked around, but she did not like any other ornament. She thought they were too plain or too big or too ugly. She decided to go home without buying anything.

When she got home, she saw her mom and dad smiling. They had a surprise for her. They showed her the tree. On the top of the tree, there was the star ornament. Sara was shocked. She asked, "How did you get it?"

Her mom and dad signed, "We saw it in the store when we went shopping. We knew you liked it, so we bought it for you. We wanted to make you happy. We love you, Sara."

Sara felt happy. She hugged her mom and dad. She signed, "I love you, too. Thank you for the star. It is the best ornament ever."

The moral of the story is: Sometimes, the things we want are already waiting for us. We just need to be patient and grateful.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park with their mom. They saw a big cage with a sign that said "Panda". They wanted to see the panda, but it was hiding behind some bamboo.

"Mom, can we go closer?" Lily asked.

"Sure, but be quiet and gentle. Pandas are shy and scared of loud noises," mom said.

They walked slowly to the cage and tried to peek through the bars. They saw a black and white furry ball curled up in a corner.

"Hello, panda. We are Lily and Ben. We want to be your friends," Ben said softly.

The panda lifted its head and looked at them with big, sad eyes. It made a low sound and moved a little.

"Poor panda. Why are you so sad?" Lily asked.

The panda pointed with its paw to a picture on the wall. It showed a green forest with many pandas playing and eating.

"Oh, you miss your home and your family," mom said. "I'm sorry, panda. You are very far away from them."

Lily and Ben felt sorry for the panda too. They wished they could help it.

"Can we give it a hug, mom?" Lily asked.

"I don't think we can, sweetie. The cage is locked and the panda might be scared of us," mom said.

"Maybe we can give it something else. Something to make it happy," Ben said.

He looked around and saw a vendor selling balloons. He ran to him and bought a red balloon. He brought it back to the cage and tied it to a bar.

"Look, panda. We got you a balloon. It's red, like your tongue. Do you like it?" Ben asked.

The panda saw the balloon and tilted its head. It reached out its paw and touched it gently. It felt the balloon bounce and float. It made a high sound and smiled.

"Wow, you made the panda happy, Ben. Good job!" Lily said.

They all watched the panda play with the balloon for a while. They felt happy too.

"Thank you, Lily and Ben. You are very kind and nice. I hope you come back and visit me again," the panda said in its own way.

They waved goodbye to the panda and left the park. They hoped the panda would find a way to go back to its home and family someday.

Lily watched as the curtain slowly opened, revealing the actors on stage. They were all dressed up in costumes, just like Lily loved to do at home. As she watched the play, Lily noticed how flexible the actors were. They could move and dance in ways she never thought possible! 

At the end of the play, the curtain closed and the actors took their final bows. Lily clapped and cheered, feeling so happy and inspired. She knew that one day, she wanted to act on stage just like the actors she saw today.

They decided to wave at the boat and see if anyone would wave back. They ran to the edge of the water and shouted, "Hello, boat! Hello, boat!"

The boat did not seem to hear them. It kept sailing on the sea. Anna and Ben felt sad. They wanted to talk to the people on the boat.

"Maybe they are busy," Anna said. "Maybe they are doing a test."

"A test?" Ben asked. "What kind of test?"

"Maybe they are testing how fast the boat can go," Anna said. "Or how strong the sail is. Or how much water they can carry."

"That sounds fun," Ben said. "I wish we could do a test like that."

They thought for a moment. Then they had an idea. They ran back to their sand castle and grabbed two sticks. They tied a towel to the sticks and made a sail. They put the sail on their sand castle and pretended it was a boat.

"Now we have a boat too," Anna said. "Let's do a test."

"OK," Ben said. "What should we test?"

"Let's test how far our boat can go," Anna said. "We can push it on the sand and see how long it takes to reach the water."

They agreed. They counted to three and pushed their boat as hard as they could. The boat slid on the sand and moved towards the water. Anna and Ben ran after it, cheering and laughing.

They reached the water just as their boat did. The waves lifted their boat and carried it away. Anna and Ben watched it with wonder. Their boat looked impressive on the sea.

"Wow, our boat is amazing," Anna said. "It went so far."

"I know," Ben said. "We did a great test."

They hugged each other and smiled. They were happy. They had made a boat and done a test. They had had a lot of fun at the beach.

"OK," Ben says. They both grab the bowl and try to lift it. But the bowl is too heavy for them. They drop the bowl on the floor. The fruit rolls everywhere. The twins hear a loud noise.

"Oh no!" Sara says. "Mom will be mad!"

They run to hide under the table. They hope Mom will not see the mess.

But Mom is in the living room. She hears the noise too. She walks to the kitchen. She sees the fruit on the floor. She sees the twins under the table.

"What happened here?" Mom asks.

Sara and Ben peek out from under the table. They look at Mom with big eyes.

"We wanted to eat the fruit," Sara says.

"But the bowl was too heavy," Ben says.

Mom shakes her head. She smiles.

"You two are crazy," Mom says. "But I love you anyway. Come here and give me a hug."

Sara and Ben crawl out from under the table. They hug Mom. Mom hugs them back.

"Next time, ask me for help," Mom says. "I will give you some fruit. But first, let's clean up this mess."

Sara and Ben nod. They help Mom pick up the fruit. They put it back in the bowl. They put the bowl on the table. They eat some fruit. They are happy. Mom is happy too.

One night, Tom and Lily wanted to play with their new spray bottles. They filled them with water and ran outside. It was a gloomy night, with dark clouds and no stars. But Tom and Lily did not care. They sprayed water at each other and laughed.

"Spray, spray, spray!" Tom shouted, as he aimed at Lily's hair.

"Stop it, Tom! You are making me wet!" Lily said, as she sprayed back at Tom's face.

They ran around the yard, spraying water everywhere. They did not see their mom coming out of the house. She was angry.

"Tom, Lily, what are you doing?" she asked, as she grabbed their spray bottles. "It is night time, you should be in bed. And look at the mess you made. You wasted water and soaked the plants and the grass. That is not good. Water is precious, you should not waste it. And plants and grass need water, but not too much. You could make them sick. You should be sorry."

Tom and Lily felt bad. They did not mean to waste water or hurt the plants and grass. They just wanted to have fun. They looked at their mom and said, "We are sorry, mom. We did not know. We will not do it again. Can we please go to bed?"

Mom sighed. She was still angry, but she also loved them. She said, "Yes, you can go to bed. But first, you have to dry yourselves and put on your pajamas. And tomorrow, you have to help me water the plants and grass properly. Do you understand?"

Tom and Lily nodded. They said, "We understand, mom. We will help you. We love you, mom."

Mom smiled. She said, "I love you too, Tom and Lily. Now, go to bed and sleep well. And remember, water is precious, you should not waste it."

Tom and Lily hugged their mom and went to bed. They learned their lesson. They never played with their spray bottles at night again. They only used them in the day, and only when they had permission. They also helped their mom water the plants and grass every day. They were good children.

Liz nodded and smiled. She was sorry, too.

The rose did not answer, but Sara felt a gentle breeze and saw the rose nod slightly. She smiled and said, "Thank you, rose. Thank you for being so lovely and for coming with me." She carefully picked the rose and held it in her hand.

She was about to go to her room, when she saw her brother Tom playing with his ball. He saw her rose and said, "Hey, Sara, what do you have there? A rose? Can I see it?"

Sara shook her head and said, "No, Tom, this is my rose. I requested it from the bush and it said yes. You can't have it. It is mine."

Tom did not listen. He grabbed the rose from Sara and said, "I want to see it. I want to smell it. I want to play with it." He pulled the rose and tore some of its petals. He threw the rose on the ground and kicked it with his foot.

Sara was very upset. She cried and said, "Tom, you are mean! You hurt my rose! You broke it! You made it sad! Give it back to me!"

Tom laughed and said, "It is just a flower, Sara. It is not alive. It does not have feelings. It is not yours. It is nobody's. It is trash."

Sara ran to her mom and told her what Tom did. Her mom was angry and said, "Tom, you are in trouble. You have to apologize to Sara and to the rose. You have to be kind and respectful to living things. You have to learn to share and to request, not to take and to break."

She made Tom pick up the rose and give it back to Sara. She hugged Sara and said, "I'm sorry, Sara. Your rose is still beautiful, even if it is hurt. You can still keep it in your room and love it. Maybe it will grow new petals and be happy again."

Sara smiled and said, "Thank you, mom. I love you and I love my rose. I hope it will be happy again too." She kissed the rose and put it in a vase with water. She hoped that the rose would forgive Tom and feel better soon.

"Sure, you can have it. We don't like spicy things." Tom says.

"Thank you. You are nice. Do you want to trade cards with me?" Ben asks.

"OK, what cards do you have?" Tom asks.

"I have a card with a snake and a card with a frog. Do you like snakes and frogs?" Ben asks.

Tom and Lily look at each other. They do not like snakes and frogs. They are scary and slimy.

"No, thank you. We don't like snakes and frogs. We like lions and zebras. We have cards with lions and zebras. We are happy with our cards." Tom says.

The rich man felt sorry for the boy and decided to give him one of his own toys. He went back to his jeep and brought out a big toy truck. The boy was so happy and thanked the rich man. From that day on, the rich man realized that owning lots of things wasn't as important as sharing what he had with others.

One day, Timmy's mom asked him to set the table for dinner. Timmy was so excited to show his mom how responsible he was, so he quickly set the table. But, he accidentally knocked over a glass of water and it spilled all over the table.

Timmy's mom was very upset and told him he couldn't have any more peaches from the tree. Timmy was sad and didn't understand why he couldn't have any more peaches. He realized that his mistake had consequences and he had to be more careful next time.

From then on, Timmy made sure to always be careful when setting the table and he never spilled anything again. However, he was still very sad that he couldn't have any more peaches from his dependable peach tree.

Moral value: The story teaches the child not to play with the phone, to be polite and respectful when talking to others, to love and appreciate their family, and to enjoy reading books.

Lila and Ben looked at the block. They saw that it was just a red block with a star on it. It was not shiny or big or soft. It was a regular block.

They felt silly and sorry. They said, "Sorry, Mom. Sorry, Lila. Sorry, Ben."

Mom smiled and hugged them. She said, "It's okay. I'm glad you said sorry. Now, why don't you share the block and play nicely together?"

Lila and Ben nodded. They gave each other half of the block. They said, "Thank you, Mom. Thank you, Lila. Thank you, Ben."

They went back to playing with their blocks. They built a big house with a star on the roof. They used their palms to pat the blocks and make them stick. They were happy and friendly. They did not weep over a regular block again.

But when they got to the tree, they saw a sign. The sign said: "Do not climb. Tree is sick. Workers will come to fix it."

Tim and Mia were sad and angry. They loved the tree. They did not want anyone to cut it or hurt it.

They saw a man with a big truck and a big saw. He was getting ready to work on the tree.

"Stop!" Tim shouted. "You can't do that! This is our tree!"

The man looked at them and smiled. "Don't worry, kids. I'm not going to cut the tree. I'm going to help it. The tree has a bad bug that makes it sick. I'm going to take away the bad bug and give the tree some medicine. Then the tree will become healthy and strong again."

"Really?" Mia asked. "You're not lying?"

"Really," the man said. "I love trees too. I want them to be happy and grow. But I need you to stay away from the tree while I work. It's not safe for you to climb it now. Can you do that for me?"

Tim and Mia nodded. They understood. They wanted the tree to be well. They decided to play somewhere else until the man was done.

They hoped the tree would become better soon. They missed their friend.
