Ben and Mia are friends. They like to play games. One day, they play a game with cards. Each card has a strip of color on it. Ben and Mia take turns to pick a card and show it to each other.

"Look, I have a red card!" Ben says.

"I have a blue card!" Mia says.

They keep playing until they have no more cards. Then they count how many cards they have.

"I have six cards!" Ben says.

"I have five cards!" Mia says.

Ben smiles. He thinks he wins the game. He says, "I have more cards than you. I win! You lose!"

Mia feels sad. She does not like to lose. She says, "That is not fair. You had more cards than me from the start. You cheated!"

Ben feels angry. He says, "I did not cheat. You are a sore loser. You are not my friend anymore!"

They both turn away from each other. They do not talk. They do not play.

A dog sees them. The dog is adorable. He has brown fur and a wagging tail. He likes to play too. He runs to Ben and Mia. He sniffs their cards. He thinks they are toys. He grabs a card from Ben and runs away.

"Hey, that is my card!" Ben shouts. He chases the dog.

The dog thinks it is a game. He runs to Mia and drops the card. He picks another card from Mia and runs away.

"Hey, that is my card!" Mia shouts. She chases the dog too.

Ben and Mia run after the dog. They laugh. They have fun. They forget about their fight. They realize that the cards are not important. The dog is more important. He is their friend.

They catch the dog. They hug him. They say, "You are a good dog. You are adorable. You made us happy. Thank you!"

The dog wags his tail. He licks their faces. He says, "Woof!"

Ben and Mia look at each other. They smile. They say, "We are sorry. We were silly. We are friends. We do not care who wins or loses. We care about each other."

They play with the dog and the cards. They share. They are happy.

The end.

Moral: Winning is not everything. Friendship is more important. Be kind and fair to others. Do not fight over silly things. Have fun and enjoy life.

One day, a clever fox was looking for food in the forest. He saw a big cave and thought there might be something tasty inside. He crept closer and sniffed the air. He smelled a bear!

The fox was scared, but he had an idea. He called out, "Hello, Mr. Bear! Do you want to play a game with me?"

The bear was sleepy and grumpy. He growled, "What game? Go away, little fox!"

The fox said, "It's a fun game. We spin around and see who gets dizzy first. If you win, you can eat me. If I win, you give me some honey."

The bear was curious and hungry. He thought he could easily beat the fox. He said, "Fine, let's play. But you go first."

The fox nodded and ran out of the cave. He spun around and around, faster and faster, until he was a blur. Then he stopped and pretended to be dizzy. He said, "Wow, that was hard. Your turn, Mr. Bear."

The bear came out of the cave and started to spin. He spun around and around, slower and slower, until he was very dizzy. He stumbled and fell to the ground. He said, "Ugh, I don't like this game. You win, little fox."

The fox smiled and ran to the cave. He found a jar of honey and took it. He said, "Thank you, Mr. Bear. You are very kind. Goodbye!" He ran away with the honey, leaving the bear confused and angry.

The fox was very clever. He tricked the bear and got some food. He enjoyed the honey and was happy. The bear was very silly. He fell for the fox's trick and lost his food. He was still dizzy and sad.

Sara said, "Tom, move the snow. Tom, make a ball. Tom, make another ball. Tom, make a face." Tom did what Sara said. But he was not happy. He wanted to make his own snowman.

Then, they saw a big hill. Sara and Tom saw other kids slide down the hill on sleds. They looked fun. Sara and Tom wanted to try. Sara said, "Tom, move the sled. Tom, put it here. Tom, sit behind me. Tom, hold on." Tom did what Sara said. But he was not happy. He wanted to go first.

They slid down the hill. It was fast and fun. But then, they saw a big tree. Sara and Tom were scared. They did not know how to stop. Sara said, "Tom, move the sled. Tom, turn it. Tom, avoid the tree." Tom tried to do what Sara said. But it was too late. They hit the tree. They fell off the sled. They were not hurt. But they were sad.

Sara and Tom looked at each other. They were quiet. Then, Sara said, "Tom, I'm sorry. I was bossy. I did not let you have fun. I did not listen to you. Can you forgive me?" Tom looked at Sara. He saw that she was sorry. He said, "Sara, I forgive you. I love you. You are my twin. But next time, can we take turns? Can we share? Can we have fun together?" Sara smiled. She said, "Tom, yes. We can take turns. We can share. We can have fun together. You are my twin. I love you too." They hugged. They were happy.

They went back to the sled. They took turns to go first. They avoided the tree. They had fun. They learned a lesson. They were not bossy. They were twins.

Ben and Mia are friends. They like to play with toys. Ben has a gray car. Mia likes the gray car. She asks Ben, "Can I borrow your gray car?"

Ben says, "No, it is mine. You have your own toys."

Mia is sad. She wants to play with the gray car. She thinks Ben is not a good friend. She goes to play with someone else.

Ben plays with his gray car alone. He is bored. He sees Mia playing with a person he does not know. They have fun. They share their toys. Ben feels lonely. He wishes he had a friend.

He goes to Mia and says, "I am sorry. I was mean. You can borrow my gray car. Do you want to play with me?"

Mia smiles. She says, "Thank you. You are a good friend. Yes, I want to play with you."

They play together. They share their toys. They are happy.

The moral of the story is: Sharing is caring. It is better to be kind and generous than selfish and greedy.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. They run and jump and laugh. They see a big slide. It is wide and shiny. They want to go on the slide.

"Let's go on the slide!" Anna says.

"Yes, let's go!" Ben says.

They run to the slide. They wait for their turn. They see a boy on the slide. He is bigger than them. He is mean. He does not let them go on the slide.

"Go away!" he says. "This is my slide!"

He pushes them. He makes them fall. He laughs. Anna and Ben are sad. They are hurt. They are miserable.

They cry. They want to go home. They see a lady. She is kind. She is the boy's mom. She sees what the boy did. She is angry.

"What are you doing?" she says. "That is not nice! You have to share the slide! You have to say sorry!"

She makes the boy get off the slide. She makes him say sorry to Anna and Ben. She hugs them. She gives them a band-aid. She tells them to go on the slide.

"Go on, have fun!" she says. "The slide is for everyone!"

Anna and Ben smile. They say thank you. They go on the slide. They have fun. They are happy. They are friends.

Sam liked trucks very much. He had many trucks in his room. Big trucks, small trucks, red trucks, blue trucks. He played with them every day. He made them go vroom vroom and beep beep.

One day, Sam saw a new truck in the street. It was a fire truck. It was shiny and loud. It had a ladder and a hose. Sam wanted to see it up close. He ran to the window and looked outside.

The fire truck stopped near a house. There was smoke coming out of the house. Sam was scared. He hoped everyone was okay. He saw some people in yellow clothes get out of the fire truck. They were firefighters. They had helmets and boots. They were brave and dependable.

The firefighters used the ladder and the hose to put out the fire. They helped the people in the house. They made sure no one was hurt. They did a good job. Sam was happy. He clapped his hands and cheered for them.

The firefighters heard Sam and waved at him. They smiled and thanked him. They said he was a good boy. They asked him if he liked trucks. Sam nodded and said yes. They said they liked trucks too. They said they had a special truck for him. They gave him a toy fire truck. It was shiny and loud. It had a ladder and a hose. Sam was very happy. He hugged the toy truck and thanked the firefighters. He said they were his heroes. He said he wanted to be a firefighter when he grew up. The firefighters said he could be anything he wanted. They said goodbye and drove away.

Sam went back to his room. He put the toy fire truck next to his other trucks. He played with them all. He made them go vroom vroom and beep beep. He pretended to put out fires and help people. He had a lot of fun. He loved trucks very much.

Tom and Dad like to play golf on Sundays. They go to a big field with many holes and flags. They hit a small ball with a stick and try to make it go in the hole. Sometimes the ball goes far, sometimes it goes near, sometimes it goes in the trees or the water. Tom and Dad laugh and have fun.

One Sunday, they meet a new friend on the field. His name is Ben and he is very good at golf. He can hit the ball very far and very straight. He shows Tom and Dad how to hold the stick and swing it. He says, "Relax your arms and your shoulders. Don't hit the ball too hard. Just let it fly."

Tom and Dad try to do what Ben says, but it is not easy. They still hit the ball in the wrong places. They feel a little sad and a little angry. Ben says, "Don't worry, golf is a hard game. You need to practice a lot. But the most important thing is to have fun. Come on, let's go to the next hole."

They walk to the next hole and see a big cart with many snacks and drinks. Ben says, "Look, this is my treat. You can have anything you want. I like the cookies and the juice. They are delicious." Tom and Dad smile and say, "Thank you, Ben. You are very kind. We like the cookies and the juice too. They are delicious."

They sit on the grass and eat and drink. They talk about golf and other things. They feel happy and relaxed. They forget about the bad shots and the hard holes. They enjoy the sun and the breeze. They make a new friend. They have a good day.

Lily was playing with her dolls in the living room. She liked to make them talk and have tea parties. She heard a noise from upstairs. It sounded like someone was crying. She wondered who it was.

She left her dolls and went to the stairs. She called out, "Who is upstairs? Why are you sad?" She heard a voice that was distant and low. It said, "It's me, Ben. I'm sad because I broke my toy car. It was my favorite."

Lily felt sorry for Ben. He was her big brother and he was usually nice to her. She climbed the stairs and went to his room. She saw him sitting on his bed, holding the pieces of his car. She said, "I'm sorry, Ben. I know you loved your car. Can I help you fix it?"

Ben looked at her and smiled a little. He said, "Thank you, Lily. You are very kind. But I don't think we can fix it. It's too broken." He sighed and put the pieces on his desk.

Lily thought for a moment. She had an idea. She said, "Maybe we can't fix it, but we can make something new with it. We can use the wheels and the lights and the stickers and make a spaceship or a robot or a castle. It will be fun and creative."

Ben liked Lily's idea. He said, "That sounds fun and creative. You are very smart, Lily. Will you help me make something new?" He got up and hugged her.

Lily nodded and hugged him back. She said, "Of course I will help you. You are my brother and I love you. And you know what? Sometimes things break, but we can always find a way to make something good out of them. That's what my teacher told me."

Ben agreed. He said, "You're right, Lily. That's a good lesson to learn. Come on, let's go downstairs and get some glue and scissors and paper and see what we can make."

They went downstairs, holding hands. They left their sadness upstairs and brought their happiness downstairs. They had fun and made something new with their broken car. They learned that they could always hear each other and help each other. They were a good team.

Ben and Mia are friends. They like to play in the park. They see a big spring. It is shiny and round. They want to jump on it.

"Can we jump on the spring?" Ben asks Mia.

"Yes, let's jump on the spring!" Mia says.

They run to the spring. They take turns to jump on it. They go up and down. They feel happy. They laugh and shout.

But there is a man near the spring. He is old and deaf. He cannot hear Ben and Mia. He is reading a book. He likes to read in the park.

Ben and Mia jump too hard. The spring makes a loud noise. It goes "boing, boing, boing". The man looks up from his book. He is angry. He does not like the noise.

"Stop jumping on the spring!" he says. "You are making too much noise!"

But Ben and Mia cannot hear him. They are having too much fun. They keep jumping on the spring.

The man gets up from his bench. He walks to the spring. He tries to make Ben and Mia stop. But they do not see him. They are too busy jumping.

The man reaches the spring. He puts his hand on it. He wants to stop it from moving. But the spring is too strong. It pushes his hand away. It makes him lose his balance. He falls to the ground.

Ben and Mia stop jumping. They see the man on the ground. They are scared. They think they hurt him.

"Are you okay?" Ben asks the man.

The man does not answer. He cannot hear Ben. He is deaf. He is also angry. He picks up his book. He walks away from the spring. He does not look at Ben and Mia.

Ben and Mia feel sorry. They did not mean to make the man angry. They did not know he was deaf. They want to say sorry. But the man is gone.

They look at the spring. They do not want to jump on it anymore. They decide to play something else. They go to the slide. They hope the man is okay. They hope he is not too angry. They hope he still likes to read in the park.

Tom and Mia are friends. They like to play with cars and trucks. They have many cars and trucks in their room. Some are big, some are small, some are red, some are blue.

One day, Tom and Mia find a new car in their room. It is a lab car. It is huge and white. It has many buttons and lights. Tom and Mia are curious. They want to see what the lab car can do.

They get inside the lab car. They see a big screen and a wheel. They see a button that says "speed". Tom pushes the button. The lab car starts to move. It moves very fast. It zooms out of their room. It zooms down the hall. It zooms past their mom and dad. It zooms out of the house.

"Wow, this is fun!" Tom says.

"Look, we are flying!" Mia says.

The lab car flies in the sky. It flies over the trees and the houses. It flies over the birds and the clouds. It flies very high and very far.

Tom and Mia are happy. They laugh and cheer. They see many things they have never seen before. They feel like they are in a dream.

But then, they see a problem. The lab car is running out of gas. The screen says "low gas". The lights blink red. The lab car starts to slow down. It starts to fall.

"Oh no, what do we do?" Tom says.

"I don't know, I'm scared!" Mia says.

They look for a button that says "stop" or "land". But they can't find it. They only see the button that says "speed". They push it again. But nothing happens. The lab car keeps falling.

They hug each other. They close their eyes. They hope for a miracle.

Then, they hear a voice. It is their mom's voice. She says "Wake up, Tom and Mia. It's time for breakfast."

Tom and Mia open their eyes. They are in their room. They are in their bed. They are not in the lab car. They are not flying. They are not falling. They are dreaming.

They look at each other. They smile. They say "That was a cool dream!"

They get out of their bed. They see the lab car in their room. It is not huge and white. It is small and yellow. It is a toy. It is not a real lab car.

They pick up the toy. They say "Thank you, lab car. You gave us a great adventure!"

They run to the kitchen. They hug their mom. They eat their breakfast. They tell their mom about their dream. They say "We love you, mom. And we love our lab car!"

One Wednesday, they were playing with the car in the park. Tim was driving and Lily was sitting next to him. They saw a big hill and decided to go up. They pushed the car hard and made loud noises. "Vroom, vroom, we are so fast!" Tim said. "Yeah, we are the best drivers!" Lily agreed.

But when they reached the top of the hill, they saw a small boy sitting on a bench. He was holding a small blue car. He looked sad and lonely. Tim and Lily paused. They felt sorry for the boy. They looked at each other and had an idea.

They rolled down the hill and stopped near the bench. They smiled at the boy and said hello. "Hi, we are Tim and Lily. What is your name?" Tim asked. "I am Ben. I like your car. It is very big and red." Ben said. "Thank you. We like your car too. It is very small and blue." Lily said.

"Do you want to play with us?" Tim offered. "We can share our cars and have more fun." Ben's eyes lit up. He nodded and smiled. He joined Tim and Lily and they played together. They drove their cars up and down the hill, around the trees and over the bridge. They laughed and talked and had a great time.

Tim and Lily were happy. They made a new friend. They learned to be humble and kind. They realized that sharing was more fun than having. They looked forward to the next Wednesday.

Lily and Max are twins. They like to play together, but sometimes they quarrel. One day, Mom makes broccoli for dinner. Lily and Max do not like broccoli. They make faces and say "yuck".

Mom says, "You have to eat your broccoli. It is good for you. It makes you strong and healthy."

Lily and Max say, "No, we don't want to. It is yucky and green. We want pizza and ice cream."

Mom says, "You can have pizza and ice cream another day. Today, you have to eat your broccoli. If you don't, you will go to bed without dessert."

Lily and Max are miserable. They do not want to go to bed without dessert. They look at each other and have an idea. They decide to stop quarreling and work together. They take their forks and pretend to eat their broccoli. But they do not eat it. They hide it under their napkins, or in their pockets, or behind their cups.

Mom does not notice. She is busy with the dishes. She thinks Lily and Max are being good. She says, "Well done, you ate your broccoli. You can have dessert now. What do you want?"

Lily and Max say, "We want chocolate cake and whipped cream."

Mom says, "Okay, you can have that. But first, let me see your plates."

Lily and Max are scared. They know Mom will find out their trick. They try to hide their plates, but it is too late. Mom sees the broccoli under the napkins, in the pockets, and behind the cups. She is angry. She says, "You did not eat your broccoli. You lied to me. You are naughty. You will not have dessert. You will go to bed right now."

Lily and Max are sad. They cry and say, "We are sorry, Mom. We do not like broccoli. Please, can we have dessert?"

Mom says, "No, you cannot. You have to learn your lesson. Maybe tomorrow, you will eat your broccoli."

Lily and Max go to bed without dessert. They hug each other and say, "We are sorry, too. We should not have quarreled. We should have eaten our broccoli. Maybe tomorrow, we will like it."

The end.

"Good goose, good goose," she said, petting the goose's head.

But then, the goose saw more bread in Lily's other hand. It wanted more. It opened its beak and honked loudly. It bit Lily's hand and pulled the bread. Lily screamed and dropped the bread. She ran back to Ben, crying.

"Ow, ow, ow! The goose bit me! The goose bit me!" she sobbed, holding her hand.

"I'm sorry, Lily. The goose was greedy. It wanted more bread. It didn't mean to hurt you," he said, trying to comfort her.

"Bad goose, bad goose!" Lily said, wiping her tears. "I don't like the white goose anymore. I like the brown ducks. They are nice and gentle."

Max heard Lily yell. He was not hurt. He was happy. He thought he touched the cloud. He smiled and said, "I did it! I did it!" He swam up and popped his head out of the water. He said, "Lily, I touched the cloud! It was wet and cold!"

Lily was angry. She said, "No, you didn't, Max. You touched the water. You were silly and dangerous. You could have drowned. You made me worry."

Max was sad. He said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I just wanted to touch the cloud. I thought it would be fun."

Lily sighed. She said, "It's okay, Max. I forgive you. But don't do that again. Clouds are not for touching. They are for looking and dreaming."

Max nodded. He said, "Okay, Lily. I won't do that again. I love you."

Lily smiled. She said, "I love you too, Max. Come on, let's play some more. But this time, let's be fish, not birds."

They hugged and kissed and swam and splashed. They were happy and safe. They looked at the cloud and saw a bunny. They laughed and said, "It's a bunny! It's a bunny!"

The mouse thought for a moment and said, "Well, Mr. Lion, I know a way to prove you are the smartest. Let's play a game. If you can catch me in three tries, then you are truly the smartest." The lion agreed and tried to catch the mouse. But the mouse was too fast and the lion missed every time.

The lion was very sad and said, "I am not the smartest animal in the forest. I could not catch the mouse." The mouse came up to the lion and said, "Mr. Lion, being smart is not about catching me. It is about knowing what is important. You should value being kind and helping others, not just being smart."

The lion learned a lesson that day. He decided to be kind and help other animals in the forest. And all the animals were happy and they all became friends.

They opened their sandwiches and took a bite. Jenny liked her cheese sandwich, but Tom did not like his ham sandwich. It was too dry and bland.

"Yuck, this is not good," Tom said. "I wish I had some ketchup or mustard."

"Maybe you can use the magic pepper," Jenny said. "Grandma said it can make any food taste good."

Tom thought that was a good idea. He opened his small bag and took out the pepper. It was red and shiny and smelled spicy. He twisted the top of the pepper and sprinkled some on his ham sandwich.

"Be careful, Tom," Jenny said. "Don't use too much. The pepper is fragile and might break."

But Tom did not listen. He wanted his sandwich to be very tasty. He twisted the pepper harder and harder, until it cracked and spilled all over his sandwich and his lap.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Tom cried. "The pepper is hot! It burns my mouth and my skin!"

Jenny and their mom and dad heard Tom's cry and ran to him. They saw the pepper broken and the sandwich ruined. They also saw Tom's red face and tears.

"Oh, Tom, what did you do?" their mom asked. "You used too much pepper. You should have listened to Jenny. The pepper is fragile and hot. You need to be gentle and careful with it."

"I'm sorry, mom," Tom said. "I wanted my sandwich to be good, but I made it bad. And I hurt myself and the pepper. Can you make it better?"

Their mom hugged Tom and gave him some water and a napkin. She wiped his mouth and his lap and kissed his cheek.

"It's okay, Tom," she said. "You made a mistake, but you learned a lesson. Next time, you will be more gentle and careful with the pepper and other things. And don't worry, the pepper is not really magic. It's just a special gift from grandma. She will understand and forgive you. And I'm sure we can find you another sandwich that you will like."

Tom nodded and hugged his mom back. He said sorry to Jenny and thanked her for her advice. He also said sorry to the pepper and put it back in his bag. He hoped it would not hurt too much.

Then they all went to find another snack and waited for their plane. They were still excited to travel and see new things. But they also remembered to be gentle and careful with their things and themselves.

"Are you okay?" the man asked. He looked at Tom's hand. It was red and sore.

"It's okay, Tom. I'm sorry too. I did not know what shock meant. Now I know. It is not fun. It is bad," Lily said.

"Sure, you can have some grapes," mom said. "But first, you have to prepare them. You have to wash them and take them off the stem."

Ben and Lily nodded. They went to the sink and turned on the water. They put the grapes in a colander and rinsed them. They used their fingers to pluck the grapes from the stem. They put the grapes in a bowl.

They were about to eat the grapes when they heard a loud roar. They turned around and saw a fierce lion in the kitchen. The lion had escaped from the zoo and was looking for food. It saw the grapes and licked its lips.

"Roar! I want those grapes!" the lion said.

Ben and Lily were scared. They ran to their mom and hid behind her. Mom grabbed a broom and waved it at the lion.

"Go away, lion! These are our grapes! You can't have them!" mom said.

The lion was angry. It growled and showed its teeth. It tried to swipe the broom with its paw. But mom was brave. She hit the lion on the nose with the broom. The lion yelped and ran away.

Ben and Lily cheered. They hugged their mom and thanked her.

"You're welcome, my sweeties. You're very brave, too. Now, let's enjoy our grapes. They're delicious and healthy," mom said.

They sat down at the table and ate the grapes. They were juicy and sweet. They were happy and safe. They loved their mom and their grapes.

Lily did not like what her mom said. She felt sad and angry. She said, "No, mom, I like to eat. I don't want to move. I want to wear my old pants. They are comfortable."

Her mom shook her head and said, "Lily, you have to listen to me. You have to take care of your body. You have to be healthy and happy. Trust me, you will feel better if you eat less and move more. And you will find new pants that are comfortable and pretty."

She only noticed when she heard a loud sound. It was her pants. They ripped. They ripped because they could not hold her anymore. They ripped because she increased and increased and increased.

Lily felt a shock. She felt a pain. She felt a shame. She looked at her pants. She looked at her belly. She looked at her mom. She looked at the people. They all looked at her. They all saw her. They all heard her.

On the day of the party, the castle was full of fun and friends. The prince, king, and queen were all very glad that their plan worked. They danced and played all day long, and they lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, in a big green forest, there was a huge insect. This insect was very strong and liked to show off. One day, it met a small ant who was carrying a tiny leaf.

The huge insect laughed at the small ant and said, "You are so weak! I can carry bigger things than you!" The small ant did not like this, but it did not say anything. It just kept walking with its tiny leaf.

The huge insect wanted to show the small ant how strong it was. So, it tried to carry a big rock. But the rock was too heavy for the insect. It tried and tried, but it could not lift the rock. The small ant saw this and said, "Sometimes, it is better to surrender and ask for help."

The huge insect felt bad and understood the small ant's words. From that day on, the insect learned to be humble and ask for help when needed. And the moral of the story is, it's okay to ask for help and we should not look down on others.

Once upon a time, in a big forest, there was a little bunny named Bobo. Bobo was very sorry because he had lost his way. He sat on the earth and began to cry.

A kind deer heard Bobo's cries and came to help. The deer said, "Why are you crying, little bunny?" Bobo looked up and said, "I'm sorry, but I'm lost. I can't find my home." The kind deer thought for a moment and then said, "Don't worry, little bunny. I will help you find your home."

The deer and Bobo walked through the forest together. They saw many animals on their way. Each time they met a new friend, Bobo would bow and say, "Hello." The animals would bow back and say, "Hello, little bunny."

Finally, they found Bobo's home. Bobo was so happy that he jumped up and down. He said, "Thank you, kind deer!" The deer smiled and said, "You're welcome, little bunny. Remember to always be kind and help others, just like I helped you."

From that day on, Bobo the bunny always tried to be kind and helpful to all his friends in the forest. And whenever he met someone new, he would always bow and say, "Hello."

After they played, the big man said, "Good job, kids! You listened to my order and were gentle with my baseball." Tim and his friends were happy. They thanked the big man and went home. They had a fun day playing baseball at the park.

Tim and Sam played with the magnet and the toy car. But then, the magnet broke because it was very fragile. Tim was sad and Sam was upset. They didn't know what to do.

Tim said, "I'm sorry, Sam. I didn't mean to break the magnet." Sam thought for a moment and said, "It's okay, Tim. We can try to fix it together." So they found some glue and put the magnet back together.

In the end, Tim and Sam were happy again. They learned to be more careful with fragile things and to always help each other when things go wrong.

The lion asked the mouse, "Why do you cry, little mouse?" The mouse said, "I lost my watch. It was my mom's watch, and I love it so much." The lion felt bad for the mouse and decided to help him. They looked everywhere for the watch. Finally, they found it under a big rock.

The lion used his mighty strength to move the rock, and the mouse got his watch back. The mouse was so happy that he stopped crying. He thanked the lion and said, "You are very kind, even though you are so mighty." The lion smiled and said, "Being strong is good, but being kind is better."

From that day on, the lion and the mouse became good friends. All the animals in the village learned that even the mighty can be kind and helpful.

The bug stayed inside the apple for a long time. The apple began to rot because the bug was eating it. One day, the bug came out of the apple and saw that the sky was blue and bright again. Amy sat on the bench and listened to the birds. She felt very happy and peaceful. She talked to the birds, "Hello, birds! I like your songs." The birds sang even louder and Amy smiled.

After a while, Amy's mom came out of the store. She saw Amy sitting on the bench, smiling and talking to the birds. She said, "Amy, did you have fun?" Amy said, "Yes, Mom! I made friends with the birds!" They both laughed and went home, feeling happy and peaceful.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Sarah and Jake. They liked to have lots of fun together, but Jake was always getting into trouble!

One day, Sarah was playing with a knife. She wasn't being very careful, and it slipped and cut her lip. Sarah started to cry and Jake felt really bad.

He told Sarah he could fix it. He held her lip open with his fingers and then looked around for something to make it better. He saw a pink flower nearby, so he cut a piece off and put it on Sarah's lip.

The flower worked. It made Sarah's lip feel much better and prettier too! From then on, Sarah and Jake were both extra careful when playing with knives.

Suddenly, a giant lion jumped out from behind the trees. He roared, saying "Foolish tiger, didn't you learn your lesson last time you went for a walk in the forest?" The tiger stood there trembling, then the lion said "Now, let's see how good you are at counting. I want you to count, from one to one hundred, three times! The tiger was so scared, but he bravely started counting. He kept going even though the lion was getting closer and closer. Eventually, he reached one hundred three times, without making a single mistake.

He was now much smaller than before and was so excited! He started to run around and giggle, something he hardly ever did! He wanted to explore the woods and all its little creatures, so he set off on his journey.

One day, a jet was up in the sky soaring. All of a sudden, the jet starting to spin and it wasn't going to stop. The jet was getting closer to the ground and was spiraling downwards. Then, a young white dove flew over and said, "Surrender! Let go and I'll catch you." The jet didn't believe the dove and continued to spin downwards. Right before the jet hit the ground, the dove flew underneath and said, "Surrender! I'll catch you." This time, the jet surrendered and the dove flew up holding the jet in its beak. The dove was so strong and flew so high with the jet that eventually, the jet was back in the sky, and the jet's journey was perfect again.

The moral of the story is to trust in others. Sometimes, asking for help can be the best thing to do and can get you to where you need to be. Surrendering and having faith can offer you the perfect journey.
